Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 10 — required installment (each column)
Fact.Description:
Form 2210 Part III line 10: "Otherwise, enter 25% (0.25) of line 9, Form 2210, in each column." One fact rather than four, because the four columns carry the SAME figure whenever Schedule AI is not used.
This fact is line 10’s "Otherwise" arm, the flat quarter. The printed line’s FIRST arm is modelled too, so line 10 proper is /form2210RequiredInstallmentColA through ColD, each a Switch on /form2210ElectsScheduleAi that reads THIS fact when box C is unchecked and Schedule AI line 27 when it is checked. Those four read this fact rather than re-deriving 25% deliberately, so the unelected population is untouched by construction. This fact also serves Schedule AI’s own printed line 24 ("Enter 25% (0.25) of line 9 ... in each column"), which is the same figure, and through line 26 it is the ceiling that keeps the annualized method from ever demanding more than the regular one.
Incomplete whenever Part I line 9 is, which is whenever the prior-year attestations are unanswered — the refusal that /form2210Penalty turns into an honest "not computed". Unrounded: the printed line gives no rounding instruction and 25% of a whole-dollar line 9 is a quarter-dollar by construction.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 11 — the WITHHOLDING half, one-fourth per payment period
Fact.Description:
The withholding component of Form 2210 Part III line 11. The printed default makes it need NO payment-date input — "For withheld federal income tax and excess social security or tier 1 RRTA, you are considered to have paid one-fourth of these amounts on each payment due date unless you can show otherwise" — so it is one-fourth of Part I line 6 in every column.
THIS IS NOT THE WHOLE OF LINE 11: /form2210Line11ColA through /form2210Line11ColD are the printed line, each adding the estimated payments that fall in its own printed window to this quarter on top of the withholding share. Nothing about the withholding arithmetic depends on whether any payment dates are answered, which is why a return with no dated payments resolves on this term alone.
EXTRACTION TRAP, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-WALKED. pdftotext interleaves i2210's two print columns, so a "one-third" sentence sits visually adjacent to this rule at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2210.pdf, page 4. That one-third belongs to item 3 of the Form 1040-NR-only modified instructions, which SKIP column (a) and therefore have three columns, not four. The general rule is one-fourth, confirmed independently by the pub's own Example 1 (lines 296-301): $4,000 withheld gives $1,000 in each of columns (a) through (d).
WITHHOLDING NEVER BUYS A SHORTER DAY COUNT, which is why it stays separated from the dated payments rather than being folded into the same collection. The Penalty Worksheet's line 1b — the only line that shortens a column's day count — excludes it by name: "Do not enter any withheld federal income tax and excess social security or tier 1 RRTA on line 1b."

Fact.Name: Box D: federal income tax actually withheld through April 15, 2025 (Form 2210 line 11, column (a))
Fact.Description: Asked only when Part II box D is checked: the federal income tax (and excess social security or tier 1 RRTA) actually withheld through April 15, 2025, the window of Form 2210 Part III column (a). A filer who treats only one kind of withholding on its actual dates, which section 6654(g)(2) allows, enters that kind on its dates and the other kind at one-fourth per column. With all three columns answered, non-negative and together no more than the whole withholding, line 11 uses them and column (d) takes the rest; otherwise line 11 keeps the one-fourth default. Unanswered changes nothing.

Fact.Name: Box D is checked and the withholding dates are established for line 11
Fact.Description: TRUE when Part II box D is checked and the three column entries /form2210WritableBoxDWithholdingColumnA through C are all answered, none is negative, and together they do not exceed the whole withholding (estimatedPayments:/form2210WithholdingTaxes), so that column (d) takes a non-negative remainder. Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 11, column (a)
Fact.Description: Line 11 column (a) = the withholding quarter + the estimated tax payments made through April 15, 2025. Equal to the withholding quarter alone whenever no dated payment exists.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 11, column (b)
Fact.Description: Line 11 column (b) = the withholding quarter + the estimated tax payments made after April 15, 2025 through column (b)'s shifted June 16, 2025 close.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 11, column (c)
Fact.Description: Line 11 column (c) = the withholding quarter + the estimated tax payments made after June 16, 2025 through September 15, 2025.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 11, column (d)
Fact.Description: Line 11 column (d) = the withholding quarter + the estimated tax payments made after September 15, 2025 through January 15, 2026.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 15, column (a)
Fact.Description: Line 15 column (a) = line 11, by the column-(a)-only rule printed on line 15 itself. The general line-15 subtraction has no operands in column (a) (lines 13 and 14 both read "the previous column").

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 17, column (a) — underpayment
Fact.Description: Line 17 column (a): "If line 10 is equal to or more than line 15, subtract line 15 from line 10." Zero when line 15 exceeds line 10 (that case goes to line 18 instead), so this is the non-negative excess of the required installment over the amount treated as paid by 04/15/25. Note the boundary is INCLUSIVE on line 10 ("equal to or more than"), which at equality yields exactly 0 — the same value the line-18 branch would give, so the two branches agree on the boundary rather than competing.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 18, column (a) — overpayment
Fact.Description: Line 18 column (a): "If line 15 is more than line 10, subtract line 10 from line 15." Zero otherwise. Carried into column (b)'s line 12/13 as the credit that rolls forward. Strictly complementary to line 17: at most one of the two is non-zero.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 13, column (b)
Fact.Description: Line 13 column (b) = line 11 + line 12, where line 12 is column (a)'s line 18 (overpayment rolled forward). The amount available to meet the 06/15/25 installment before any earlier shortfall is charged against it.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 14, column (b)
Fact.Description: Line 14 column (b) = "Add the amounts on lines 16 and 17 in the previous column" — column (a)'s line 16 plus its line 17. Column (a)'s line 16 is structurally 0 (see the column-(a) note above), so this is column (a)'s underpayment alone. This is the mechanic by which a payment is applied FIRST to an older shortfall: "Your payments are applied first to any underpayment balance on an earlier installment even if you designate a payment for a later period" (i2210, Section B).

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 15, column (b)
Fact.Description: Line 15 column (b) = line 13 − line 14, floored at zero ("If zero or less, enter -0-"). What is left of the 06/15/25 period's money after the earlier shortfall has been satisfied.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 16, column (b)
Fact.Description: Line 16 column (b): "If line 15 is zero, subtract line 13 from line 14. Otherwise, enter -0-." The still-unsatisfied part of the earlier shortfall, carried into column (c)'s line 14. Modelled as the floored difference line 14 − line 13: because line 15 is itself max(0, line 13 − line 14), "line 15 is zero" holds exactly when line 14 is at least line 13, which is exactly when that floored difference is the printed subtraction — and where the printed rule says "-0-" the floor already gives 0. The two forms are identical on every input, not merely on the tested ones.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 17, column (b) — underpayment
Fact.Description: Line 17 column (b) = line 10 − line 15, floored at zero.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 18, column (b) — overpayment
Fact.Description: Line 18 column (b) = line 15 − line 10, floored at zero. Rolls forward into column (c)'s line 12/13.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 13, column (c)

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 14, column (c)

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 16, column (c)

Fact.Name: Penalty Worksheet line 13, column (d) — 90 days
Fact.Description:
Column (d)'s underpayment charged from its 01/15/26 due date to 04/15/26. This is column (d)'s only cell: the three earlier rate periods all closed before its due date, which Table 2 prints as dashes.
SECTION 6654(h) EMPTIES THIS CELL AND ONLY THIS CELL. A filer who files the return and pays the tax due in full on or before 31 January 2026 owes no addition to tax "with respect to any underpayment of the 4TH required installment" - the fourth, not the earlier three. Column (d) IS the fourth installment and this is its only cell, so zeroing it is the whole of the relief; the twelve-cell sum keeps every column (a), (b) and (c) charge, including the parts of them that run through rate period 4. Complete-safe FALSE upstream: an unanswered claim charges the cell in full.

Fact.Name: Table 4-1 day number for this payment - the days from 04/15/25 to the date it was made
Fact.Description:
This payment's date as Table 4-1's day number: 0 for April 15, 2025, 365 for April 15, 2026, and the printed cell in between. The table is a calendar of consecutive integers, so the thirteen cases below are its month offsets plus the day of the month, and every offset is checked against the printed cell for the FIRST and LAST day of its month (May 1 = 16 and May 31 = 46; June 1 = 47 and June 30 = 76; and so on to April 1, 2026 = 351 and April 15, 2026 = 365). Table 4-1's own worked example is reproduced: "The payment due date is June 15 (61). The payment was made on November 4 (203)" - June 15 is 15+46 and November 4 is 4+199.
THE TWO CLAMPS ARE NOT APPROXIMATIONS. A date on or before April 15, 2025 becomes 0 because no column's due date falls before it, so it can never appear on any line 1b; the printed table has no cell for it and none is needed. A date after April 15, 2026 becomes 365 because the worksheet's day counts all end at "04/15/26, whichever is earlier", so such a payment carries a zero-day credit.
JUNE 16, 2025 IS DAY 61 AND NOT DAY 62, and that is the printed weekend Note rather than a rounding. June 15, 2025 is a Sunday and June 16 a Monday, and a payment made on the next business day "is considered made on the due date". Being considered made ON June 15 has two consequences that must agree, and here they do: it is NOT "after the date at the top of" column (b), so it cannot appear on column (b)'s line 1b, and its day count is 61. The shipped estimatedPayments:/form2210DatedEstimatedPayments/*/amountInColumnB already applies the same shift on the line 11 side, so a June 16 payment reduces column (b)'s underpayment rather than crediting column (b)'s line 1b - which is exactly the netting/credit boundary this block's arithmetic depends on.
UNANSWERED IS A REFUSAL, NOT A ZERO. The cases are exhaustive comparisons with no True fallback, so a row whose date is unanswered resolves INCOMPLETE and that Incompleteness propagates - the same deliberate refusal the four ../amountInColumn* facts carry, and for the same reason: a payment silently dated day 0 would be credited nothing and the penalty would be overstated.

Fact.Name: This payment's amount when it was made on or before slot 1's payment date
Fact.Description:
The indicator that builds PAID(t) for slot 1: this row's amount when its Table 4-1 day number is on or before slot 1's, and zero otherwise. Summed over the collection it is the total of the payments made on or before slot 1's date.
THE PAIR IS THE POINT. The "Through" member tests "at or before" and the "Before" member tests "strictly before", so their difference is the total paid ON slot 1's own date - which is how the credit for a date shared by two payments is computed once rather than twice. See /form2210Line1bSlot1Contribution for the representative rule that spends it.
A SENTINEL SLOT COSTS NOTHING. When the collection holds fewer than 1 payments, /form2210Line1bSlot1Day is 9999 and both members collect every row, so the two sums are equal and slot 1 contributes zero.

The "Through" member tests "at or before" and the "Before" member tests "strictly before", so their difference is the total paid ON slot 8's own date - which is how the credit for a date shared by two payments is computed once rather than twice. See /form2210Line1bSlot8Contribution for the representative rule that spends it.
A SENTINEL SLOT COSTS NOTHING. When the collection holds fewer than 8 payments, /form2210Line1bSlot8Day is 9999 and both members collect every row, so the two sums are equal and slot 8 contributes zero.

Fact.Name: How many dated estimated payments the return lists
Fact.Description: The size of estimatedPayments:/form2210DatedEstimatedPayments, with the unanswered-collection firewall the whole module uses: CollectionSize over a collection that was never answered is not a Complete zero, and letting that reach the slot machinery would withdraw penalties this dictionary already computes. An unanswered collection counts zero.

Fact.Name: The dated payment list fits the sixteen hoisted slots
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the return lists at most sixteen dated estimated payments, which is the number of slots the line 1b machinery below hoists. It is the fence that keeps this module from computing a credit it can only partly see: the payment TOTALS are collection sums and stay exact at any length, but the credit must be evaluated once per distinct payment DATE, and only sixteen dates are addressable.
SIXTEEN IS THIS DICTIONARY'S CAPACITY, NOT THE FORM'S. i2210's Table 1 grid holds SIX entries - three printed rows, each carrying two Date/Payment-amount pairs - so a return with seven or more dated payments has already overflowed the paper table this collection models. The slots beyond six are headroom, not a claim.
WHAT A SEVENTEENTH PAYMENT GETS, WHEN THE LINE 1b CREDIT IS REQUIRED: /form2210Penalty resolves INCOMPLETE, so Form 1040 line 38 is left blank - the form's own "the IRS will figure it and send you a bill" default. That is a refusal by incompleteness and not a knockout - those returns file correctly today.
AND IT IS NOT CONSULTED WHEN IT CANNOT MATTER. /form2210Penalty reads it inside an Any with Not(/form2210Line1bCreditWouldBeRequired): when no column has both an underpayment and a payment made after its own due date, every line 1b entry is empty, the credit is provably zero at any list length, and a long list is computed rather than refused. THE PROOF: a credit is non-zero at date t only if some column whose due date precedes t still carries an underpayment, and that column is then exactly a column with both an underpayment and a payment made after its own due date. The arm needs a COMPLETE zero and not merely a correct one, because an Incomplete credit would poison /form2210PenaltyWorksheetTotal and withdraw a penalty that computes today; the payment sums are CollectionSums over the whole collection and an item beyond the sixteenth sits in no slot, so nothing goes Incomplete.
AN UNANSWERED COLLECTION IS WITHIN CAPACITY, because it holds no payments at all.

Fact.Name: Line 1b demand ceiling for a payment made after column (a)'s due date
Fact.Description:
The total of the Section A line 17 underpayments of column (a) alone - the only column whose 04/15/25 due date falls before a payment made in column (b)'s window: the most that the Penalty Worksheet's line 1b can ever credit to a payment made after column (a)'s due date, because line 1b is capped at each column's own line 1a and takes only payments made after the date at the top of the column.
THIS IS DEM(t) FOR ONE BAND OF DATES, in the block note's notation. It reads the SHIPPED line 17 facts, which already have every netted dollar subtracted - a payment that reduced a column's line 15 is not in that column's underpayment and therefore is not in this ceiling. That is precisely what makes the clamped recurrence free of the double-count the block note describes.

COLUMN (d) DROPS OUT UNDER SECTION 6654(h), and leaving it in would be a SECOND double-count of exactly the kind the paragraph above exists to prevent. When the January-31 rule applies, /form2210PenaltyColDPeriod4 is already $0 - column (d)'s underpayment carries no charge at all - so a payment made after 15 January that this ceiling let line 1b credit against column (d) would subtract, from the other columns' cells, a charge that had already been forgiven. Fact.Name: Whether a payment was made with the 2025 balance-due return
Amount paid with the 2025 balance-due return
Fact.Description: The amount of the payment made with the 2025 balance-due return. Required and positive when /writableForm2210BalanceDuePaymentWasMade is Yes. Kept separate from the estimated-tax payment collection so it does not alter Form 1040 line 26 reconciliation.

Fact.Name: Date filed or to be filed with the 2025 balance-due return
Fact.Description: The date filed or to be filed, used as the date of the balance-due return payment. The graph caps it at April 15, 2026 when the return is filed later. Required when /writableForm2210BalanceDuePaymentWasMade is Yes.

Fact.Name: Balance-due return payment attestation, defaulting to No
Fact.Description: An unanswered Yes/No answer is treated as No. This preserves the pre-existing penalty result for returns that do not answer the new balance-due question.

Fact.Name: Balance-due return payment amount, or zero when none was made
Fact.Description: Uses the entered amount only when the filer says a balance-due return payment was made. A Yes with no amount remains incomplete rather than silently becoming zero.

Fact.Name: Balance-due payment included in line 11 through January 15, 2026
Fact.Description: The separate balance-due payment is part of cumulative line 11 through column (d)'s January 15 due date only when its filing date is on or before that date. This is the dated-payment threshold used to keep a January 1-15 payment from being applied to column (d) before its due date.

Fact.Name: Table 4-1 day number of the balance-due return payment
Fact.Description: The balance-due payment date as a day number from April 15, 2025. A payment after April 15, 2026 is treated as paid on April 15, 2026, the worksheet endpoint. No payment maps to day 365 and earns no credit. When the filer says Yes but leaves the date blank, this fact stays incomplete.

Fact.Name: Whether the balance-due return payment inputs are complete and valid
Fact.Description: No payment is valid when the question is unanswered or No. A Yes requires a positive amount and a filing date on or after January 1, 2026. A later date is valid and is capped to April 15, 2026 for the worksheet.

Fact.Name: Balance-due return payment inputs need an answer
Fact.Description: Signals that a declared balance-due return payment is missing a positive amount or a usable date, and blocks submission directly. Without a submission block, an invalid Yes answer resolves this guard true while the penalty computation it should refuse drops to Incomplete on the missing input; a downstream leg that turns an Incomplete penalty into a computed zero would then file the return with the entire penalty silently waived. This is a data-validation guard, not a scope limit: the filer supplies a positive amount and a usable date, and the penalty computes normally.

Fact.Name: Estimated tax payments made on or before the balance-due return payment date
Fact.Description: PAID(t) for the balance-due payment: the sum of dated estimated payments made by its date. It evaluates all sixteen named dated-payment slots; the existing Form 2210 slot-capacity fact refuses a longer collection when a day-count credit is needed.

Fact.Name: Cumulative line 1b credit after estimated payments through the balance-due payment date
Fact.Description: C(t) evaluates the same capped credit after the estimated payments made on or before the balance-due payment date.

Fact.Name: Cumulative line 1b credit after the balance-due return payment
Fact.Description: C(t) after the dated estimated payments and the separate balance-due return payment. The balance-due amount joins the cumulative threshold for the payment window it actually reached; because this is the final line 11 period, the total threshold includes the balance-due amount. This caps cumulative line 1b credit at actual line 17 underpayments and preserves the installment-date boundaries.

Fact.Name: Line 1b credit caused by the balance-due return payment
Fact.Description: The incremental cumulative credit from the balance-due payment, equal to C(t) after that payment minus C(t) after the estimated payments already made by then. This difference credits a same-day group only once and caps the payment at the remaining line 17 underpayment in oldest-installment-first order.

Fact.Name: Dollar-day line 1b credit from the balance-due return payment
Fact.Description: The balance-due payment's incremental line 1b credit multiplied by the number of days from its capped payment date through April 15, 2026. An invalid Yes answer leaves this fact incomplete so the penalty cannot silently treat a declared payment as zero.

Fact.Name: The Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) estimated-tax credit, as a line 1b payment dated January 15, 2026
Fact.Description: estimatedPayments:/estateTrustK1CreditForEstimatedTaxes, the credit an estate or trust passed to the beneficiary under IRC 643(g), which the statute treats as the beneficiary's estimated tax payment made on January 15 following the year. It already sits in column (d)'s total; this fact makes it a dated payment of the Penalty Worksheet's line 1b walk too, so it is applied, in date order, first to any underpayment still open in an earlier column, exactly as a dated payment made that day would be. Complete $0 on a return with no Form 1041 K-1.

Fact.Name: This payment's amount when it was made on or before January 15, 2026
Fact.Description: This row's amount when its Table 4-1 day number is on or before 275 (January 15, 2026), and zero otherwise; summed over the collection it is the dated payments that the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) estimated-tax credit's line 1b computation treats as on or before that credit. The two cases are mutually exclusive so an undecidable date stays Incomplete.

Fact.Name: This payment's amount when it was made before January 15, 2026
Fact.Description: This row's amount when its Table 4-1 day number is before 275 (January 15, 2026), and zero otherwise; summed over the collection it is the dated payments that the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) estimated-tax credit's line 1b computation treats as before that credit. The two cases are mutually exclusive so an undecidable date stays Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Payments counted on or before the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) estimated-tax credit's date
Fact.Description: The dated estimated payments made on or before January 15, 2026, plus the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) estimated-tax credit itself. With its companion it brackets the credit's own date, the same Through and Before pair each named slot uses, so the difference of the two cumulative credits is the line 1b credit earned on that date, the K-1 credit and any dated payment of the same day together. Complete $0 on an unanswered collection.

Fact.Name: Payments counted before the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) estimated-tax credit's date
Fact.Description: The dated estimated payments made before January 15, 2026. With its companion it brackets the credit's own date, the same Through and Before pair each named slot uses, so the difference of the two cumulative credits is the line 1b credit earned on that date, the K-1 credit and any dated payment of the same day together. Complete $0 on an unanswered collection.

Fact.Name: Cumulative line 1b credit after the payments made on or before January 15, 2026, the K-1 credit included
Fact.Description: The cumulative line 1b credit function each named slot uses, evaluated at the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) estimated-tax credit's date with that credit counted.

Fact.Name: Cumulative line 1b credit after the payments made before January 15, 2026
Fact.Description: The same cumulative credit function evaluated just before the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) estimated-tax credit's date.

Fact.Name: The line 1b credit earned on January 15, 2026 when a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) estimated-tax credit is present, in dollar-days
Fact.Description: When the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) estimated-tax credit is positive, the credit earned on January 15, 2026 (the K-1 credit and any dated payment made that same day, which the named slots then leave to this fact) weighted by the 90 days to April 15, 2026; $0 otherwise, which leaves every return without that credit exactly as before.

Fact.Name: The 1st dated estimated payment, addressed by position
Fact.Description: Position 0 of estimatedPayments:/form2210DatedEstimatedPayments, hoisted so that module-level facts can read one payment's date. The engine has no operator that gives a collection item its OWN position, so a per-item running total is not expressible; IndexOf with a CONSTANT index is the inverse lookup, and it is what makes the line 1b credit a dictionary computation rather than an engine change. Out of range it resolves INCOMPLETE rather than raising, and every reader below is a Switch guarded on /form2210DatedPaymentCount so the out-of-range arm is never forced.

Fact.Name: Table 4-1 day number of slot 1's payment, or 9999 when the slot is empty
Fact.Description:
Slot 1's payment date as a Table 4-1 day number, or the sentinel 9999 when the return lists fewer than 1 dated payments.
THE SENTINEL IS INERT BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a special case downstream. No real payment can reach 9999 - /form2210DatedEstimatedPayments/*/form2210PaymentDayNumber clamps every date into 0..365 - so at 9999 both of slot 1's payment sums collect the whole collection, their difference is zero, and slot 1's contribution is zero whatever the underpayments are. The Switch is lazy, so the out-of-range IndexOf in the first arm is never evaluated.

Fact.Name: Dated estimated payments made on or before slot 1's payment date
Fact.Description:
PAID(t) at slot 1's date, the inclusive side of the pair. Carries the module's unanswered-collection firewall: a CollectionSum over a collection that was never answered is not a Complete zero, and that Incompleteness would reach /form2210Penalty and withdraw the penalties this dictionary already computes.
IT SUMS THE WHOLE COLLECTION, not the sixteen slots, so it stays exact at any list length. Only the number of DATES at which the credit is evaluated is bounded, and /form2210DatedPaymentsWithinSlotCapacity is the fence for that.

Fact.Name: Dated estimated payments made strictly before slot 1's payment date
Fact.Description:
PAID(t) at slot 1's date, the strict side of the pair. Carries the module's unanswered-collection firewall: a CollectionSum over a collection that was never answered is not a Complete zero, and that Incompleteness would reach /form2210Penalty and withdraw the penalties this dictionary already computes.
IT SUMS THE WHOLE COLLECTION, not the sixteen slots, so it stays exact at any list length. Only the number of DATES at which the credit is evaluated is bounded, and /form2210DatedPaymentsWithinSlotCapacity is the fence for that.

Fact.Name: Cumulative line 1b credit after the payments made on or before slot 1's date
Fact.Description:
C(t) evaluated at slot 1's date, including the payments made on that date: the smallest of the five band terms derived in the block note,
min over bands b of ( DEMcum(b) + max( 0, PAID(t) - PAIDcum(b) ) )
with band 0 (payments made through April 15, 2025) contributing a demand of zero, because no column's due date precedes them.
WHY THE max(0, ...) IS NOT COSMETIC. A band whose window closes AFTER slot 1's date has collected payments that PAID(t) does not count; without the floor its term would go negative and cut the minimum below the true credit. With the floor such a band contributes exactly its own demand ceiling, which is never smaller than the answer. A band with no payment in it is harmless for the mirror-image reason: its term is at least the term of the nearest earlier band that does have one.

Fact.Name: Cumulative line 1b credit after the payments made strictly before slot 1's date
Fact.Description:
C(t) evaluated at slot 1's date, excluding the payments made on that date: the smallest of the five band terms derived in the block note,
min over bands b of ( DEMcum(b) + max( 0, PAID(t) - PAIDcum(b) ) )
with band 0 (payments made through April 15, 2025) contributing a demand of zero, because no column's due date precedes them.
WHY THE max(0, ...) IS NOT COSMETIC. A band whose window closes AFTER slot 1's date has collected payments that PAID(t) does not count; without the floor its term would go negative and cut the minimum below the true credit. A band with no payment in it is harmless for the mirror-image reason: its term is at least the term of the nearest earlier band that does have one.

Fact.Name: Slot 1's share of the line 1b credit, in dollar-days
Fact.Description:
The credit earned by the payments made ON slot 1's date, weighted by the days from that date to 04/15/26. In the block note's notation this is Q(i) x (365 - t(i)), and the sum of the sixteen slots is the whole second term of the penalty formula.
THE CREDIT FOR A DATE IS THE DIFFERENCE OF TWO CUMULATIVE FIGURES, C(t) minus C(t-), because C is a step function that only rises when a payment lands. Taking the difference rather than the payment's own amount is what applies the clamp: a payment arriving when the eligible columns' underpayments are already fully credited moves C not at all and earns nothing, which is the printed "Don't enter more than the underpayment amount on line 1a".
THE REPRESENTATIVE RULE. Slot 1 is always the representative of its own date, so it carries no representative test; slots 2 and later do.
THE WEIGHT IS FLOORED AT ZERO so the empty-slot sentinel cannot go negative; on a real payment the day number never exceeds 365 and the floor is not reached.

Fact.Name: Cumulative line 1b credit after the payments made strictly before slot 3's date
Fact.Description:
C(t) evaluated at slot 3's date, excluding the payments made on that date: the smallest of the five band terms derived in the block note,
min over bands b of ( DEMcum(b) + max( 0, PAID(t) - PAIDcum(b) ) )
with band 0 (payments made through April 15, 2025) contributing a demand of zero, because no column's due date precedes them.
WHY THE max(0, ...) IS NOT COSMETIC. A band whose window closes AFTER slot 3's date has collected payments that PAID(t) does not count; without the floor its term would go negative and cut the minimum below the true credit. With the floor such a band contributes exactly its own demand ceiling, which is never smaller than the answer. A band with no payment in it is harmless for the mirror-image reason: its term is at least the term of the nearest earlier band that does have one.

Fact.Name: Slot 3's share of the line 1b credit, in dollar-days
Fact.Description:
The credit earned by the payments made ON slot 3's date, weighted by the days from that date to 04/15/26. In the block note's notation this is Q(i) x (365 - t(i)), and the sum of the sixteen slots is the whole second term of the penalty formula.
THE CREDIT FOR A DATE IS THE DIFFERENCE OF TWO CUMULATIVE FIGURES, C(t) minus C(t-), because C is a step function that only rises when a payment lands. Taking the difference rather than the payment's own amount is what applies the clamp: a payment arriving when the eligible columns' underpayments are already fully credited moves C not at all and earns nothing, which is the printed "Don't enter more than the underpayment amount on line 1a".
THE REPRESENTATIVE RULE. Slot 3 pays only when no EARLIER slot shares its date. Two payments made on the same day produce the same two credit figures and the same weight, so without this test the day's credit would be counted once per tied payment. The rule assigns it to the lowest-numbered slot at that date and zero to the rest, which is exact rather than apportioned - the printed weight (365 - t) is identical for tied payments, so how the credit divides among them cannot change the total.
THE WEIGHT IS FLOORED AT ZERO so the empty-slot sentinel cannot go negative; on a real payment the day number never exceeds 365 and the floor is not reached.

Fact.Name: The 4th dated estimated payment, addressed by position
Fact.Description: Position 3 of estimatedPayments:/form2210DatedEstimatedPayments, hoisted so that module-level facts can read one payment's date. The engine has no operator that gives a collection item its OWN position, so a per-item running total is not expressible; IndexOf with a CONSTANT index is the inverse lookup, and it is what makes the line 1b credit a dictionary computation rather than an engine change. Out of range it resolves INCOMPLETE rather than raising, and every reader below is a Switch guarded on /form2210DatedPaymentCount so the out-of-range arm is never forced.

Fact.Name: Table 4-1 day number of slot 4's payment, or 9999 when the slot is empty
Fact.Description:
Slot 4's payment date as a Table 4-1 day number, or the sentinel 9999 when the return lists fewer than 4 dated payments.
THE SENTINEL IS INERT BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a special case downstream. No real payment can reach 9999 - /form2210DatedEstimatedPayments/*/form2210PaymentDayNumber clamps every date into 0..365 - so at 9999 both of slot 4's payment sums collect the whole collection, their difference is zero, and slot 4's contribution is zero whatever the underpayments are. The Switch is lazy, so the out-of-range IndexOf in the first arm is never evaluated.

Fact.Name: Dated estimated payments made on or before slot 4's payment date
Fact.Description:
PAID(t) at slot 4's date, the inclusive side of the pair. Carries the module's unanswered-collection firewall: a CollectionSum over a collection that was never answered is not a Complete zero, and that Incompleteness would reach /form2210Penalty and withdraw the penalties this dictionary already computes.
IT SUMS THE WHOLE COLLECTION, not the sixteen slots, so it stays exact at any list length. Only the number of DATES at which the credit is evaluated is bounded, and /form2210DatedPaymentsWithinSlotCapacity is the fence for that.

The indicator that builds PAID(t) for slot 9: this row's amount when its Table 4-1 day number is on or before slot 9's, and zero otherwise. Summed over the collection it is the total of the payments made on or before slot 9's date.
THE PAIR IS THE POINT. The "Through" member tests "at or before" and the "Before" member tests "strictly before", so their difference is the total paid ON slot 9's own date - which is how the credit for a date shared by two payments is computed once rather than twice. See /form2210Line1bSlot9Contribution for the representative rule that spends it.
A SENTINEL SLOT COSTS NOTHING. When the collection holds fewer than 8 payments, /form2210Line1bSlot9Day is 9999 and both members collect every row, so the two sums are equal and slot 9 contributes zero.

Fact.Name: The 9th dated estimated payment, addressed by position
Fact.Description: Position 8 of estimatedPayments:/form2210DatedEstimatedPayments, hoisted so that module-level facts can read one payment's date. The engine has no operator that gives a collection item its OWN position, so a per-item running total is not expressible; IndexOf with a CONSTANT index is the inverse lookup, and it is what makes the line 1b credit a dictionary computation rather than an engine change. Out of range it resolves INCOMPLETE rather than raising, and every reader below is a Switch guarded on /form2210DatedPaymentCount so the out-of-range arm is never forced.

Fact.Name: Table 4-1 day number of slot 9's payment, or 9999 when the slot is empty
Fact.Description:
Slot 9's payment date as a Table 4-1 day number, or the sentinel 9999 when the return lists fewer than 9 dated payments.
THE SENTINEL IS INERT BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a special case downstream. No real payment can reach 9999 - /form2210DatedEstimatedPayments/*/form2210PaymentDayNumber clamps every date into 0..365 - so at 9999 both of slot 9's payment sums collect the whole collection, their difference is zero, and slot 9's contribution is zero whatever the underpayments are. The Switch is lazy, so the out-of-range IndexOf in the first arm is never evaluated.

Fact.Name: Dated estimated payments made on or before slot 9's payment date
Fact.Description:
PAID(t) at slot 9's date, the inclusive side of the pair. Carries the module's unanswered-collection firewall: a CollectionSum over a collection that was never answered is not a Complete zero, and that Incompleteness would reach /form2210Penalty and withdraw the penalties this dictionary already computes.
IT SUMS THE WHOLE COLLECTION, not the sixteen slots, so it stays exact at any list length. Only the number of DATES at which the credit is evaluated is bounded, and /form2210DatedPaymentsWithinSlotCapacity is the fence for that.

Fact.Name: Dated estimated payments made strictly before slot 9's payment date
Fact.Description:
PAID(t) at slot 9's date, the strict side of the pair. Carries the module's unanswered-collection firewall: a CollectionSum over a collection that was never answered is not a Complete zero, and that Incompleteness would reach /form2210Penalty and withdraw the penalties this dictionary already computes.
IT SUMS THE WHOLE COLLECTION, not the sixteen slots, so it stays exact at any list length. Only the number of DATES at which the credit is evaluated is bounded, and /form2210DatedPaymentsWithinSlotCapacity is the fence for that.

Fact.Name: Cumulative line 1b credit after the payments made on or before slot 9's date
Fact.Description:
C(t) evaluated at slot 9's date, including the payments made on that date: the smallest of the five band terms derived in the block note,
min over bands b of ( DEMcum(b) + max( 0, PAID(t) - PAIDcum(b) ) )
with band 0 (payments made through April 15, 2025) contributing a demand of zero, because no column's due date precedes them.
WHY THE max(0, ...) IS NOT COSMETIC. A band whose window closes AFTER slot 9's date has collected payments that PAID(t) does not count; without the floor its term would go negative and cut the minimum below the true credit. With the floor such a band contributes exactly its own demand ceiling, which is never smaller than the answer. A band with no payment in it is harmless for the mirror-image reason: its term is at least the term of the nearest earlier band that does have one.

Fact.Name: Cumulative line 1b credit after the payments made strictly before slot 9's date
Fact.Description:
C(t) evaluated at slot 9's date, excluding the payments made on that date: the smallest of the five band terms derived in the block note,
min over bands b of ( DEMcum(b) + max( 0, PAID(t) - PAIDcum(b) ) )
with band 0 (payments made through April 15, 2025) contributing a demand of zero, because no column's due date precedes them.

Fact.Name: Slot 9's share of the line 1b credit, in dollar-days
Fact.Description:
The credit earned by the payments made ON slot 9's date, weighted by the days from that date to 04/15/26. In the block note's notation this is Q(i) x (365 - t(i)), and the sum of the sixteen slots is the whole second term of the penalty formula.
THE CREDIT FOR A DATE IS THE DIFFERENCE OF TWO CUMULATIVE FIGURES, C(t) minus C(t-), because C is a step function that only rises when a payment lands. Taking the difference rather than the payment's own amount is what applies the clamp: a payment arriving when the eligible columns' underpayments are already fully credited moves C not at all and earns nothing, which is the printed "Don't enter more than the underpayment amount on line 1a".
THE REPRESENTATIVE RULE. Slot 9 pays only when no EARLIER slot shares its date. Two payments made on the same day produce the same two credit figures and the same weight, so without this test the day's credit would be counted once per tied payment. The rule assigns it to the lowest-numbered slot at that date and zero to the rest, which is exact rather than apportioned - the printed weight (365 - t) is identical for tied payments, so how the credit divides among them cannot change the total.
THE WEIGHT IS FLOORED AT ZERO so the empty-slot sentinel cannot go negative; on a real payment the day number never exceeds 365 and the floor is not reached.

THE PAIR IS THE POINT. Fact.Description:

Fact.Name: Dated estimated payments made on or before slot 13's payment date
Fact.Description:
PAID(t) at slot 13's date, the inclusive side of the pair. Carries the module's unanswered-collection firewall: a CollectionSum over a collection that was never answered is not a Complete zero, and that Incompleteness would reach /form2210Penalty and withdraw the penalties this dictionary already computes.

Fact.Name: Dated estimated payments made strictly before slot 13's payment date

Fact.Name: Cumulative line 1b credit after the payments made on or before slot 13's date
Fact.Description:
C(t) evaluated at slot 13's date, including the payments made on that date: the smallest of the five band terms derived in the block note,
min over bands b of ( DEMcum(b) + max( 0, PAID(t) - PAIDcum(b) ) )
with band 0 (payments made through April 15, 2025) contributing a demand of zero, because no column's due date precedes them.
WHY THE max(0, ...) IS NOT COSMETIC. A band whose window closes AFTER slot 13's date has collected payments that PAID(t) does not count; without the floor its term would go negative and cut the minimum below the true credit. With the floor such a band contributes exactly its own demand ceiling, which is never smaller than the answer. A band with no payment in it is harmless for the mirror-image reason: its term is at least the term of the nearest earlier band that does have one.

Fact.Name: Slot 13's share of the line 1b credit, in dollar-days
Fact.Description:
The credit earned by the payments made ON slot 13's date, weighted by the days from that date to 04/15/26. In the block note's notation this is Q(i) x (365 - t(i)), and the sum of the sixteen slots is the whole second term of the penalty formula.
THE CREDIT FOR A DATE IS THE DIFFERENCE OF TWO CUMULATIVE FIGURES, C(t) minus C(t-), because C is a step function that only rises when a payment lands. Taking the difference rather than the payment's own amount is what applies the clamp: a payment arriving when the eligible columns' underpayments are already fully credited moves C not at all and earns nothing, which is the printed "Don't enter more than the underpayment amount on line 1a".
THE REPRESENTATIVE RULE. Slot 13 pays only when no EARLIER slot shares its date. Two payments made on the same day produce the same two credit figures and the same weight, so without this test the day's credit would be counted once per tied payment. The rule assigns it to the lowest-numbered slot at that date and zero to the rest, which is exact rather than apportioned - the printed weight (365 - t) is identical for tied payments, so how the credit divides among them cannot change the total.
THE WEIGHT IS FLOORED AT ZERO so the empty-slot sentinel cannot go negative; on a real payment the day number never exceeds 365 and the floor is not reached.

Fact.Name: Penalty Worksheet line 1b - the whole day-count credit, in dollar-days
Fact.Description:
The sum over every payment of the amount that landed on some column's line 1b, each weighted by the days from the payment date to 04/15/26. It is the second term of the penalty formula derived in the block note above, and it is what shortens the twelve Table 2 day counts to the counts the worksheet's lines 3, 6, 9 and 12 actually ask for.
THE UNIT IS DOLLAR-DAYS, deliberately, and this fact is not a dollar figure a filer would recognise. It exists as a named fact because it is the ONE number that separates this module's twelve constant cells from the worksheet's per-payment computation, and because every witness in the regression net pins it directly. /form2210Line1bPenaltyCredit below converts it to dollars at the printed 0.07/365.
WHY IT IS ONE AGGREGATE AND NOT TWELVE CELLS. The worksheet computes a separate figure per column per rate period, but all four TY2025 rate periods carry the same 0.07 multiplier, so the four-period split telescopes into a single day count per column and the per-column credits sum without interacting. The block note states the collapse and names it as the thing a TY2026 lift must re-check.
ZERO IS THE NORMAL ANSWER. Every return with no dated payment collection resolves this at exactly zero - all sixteen slots sit at the 9999 sentinel - so this fact is free of charge for the returns whose penalty this dictionary already computes, and the penalty they are handed does not move.
THE BALANCE-DUE RETURN PAYMENT contributes its incremental line 1b amount here, weighted to the same April 15, 2026 endpoint; it is not part of the reconciled estimated-payment collection.

Fact.Name: The line 1b credit in dollars - the amount the twelve Table 2 cells overstate
Fact.Description:
The dollar-day credit at the worksheet's printed rate: dollar-days x 0.07 / 365, the same multiplier and divisor the twelve cells above apply to their own dollar-days. It is subtracted from the worksheet total at /form2210PenaltyWorksheetTotal.
IT CAN NEVER EXCEED THE GROSS, and the proof is short enough to state rather than fence. Every dollar this credits is a dollar of some column's line 17 that the gross charges for 365 - D(c) days and that this credits for only 365 - t(i) days, where t(i) is strictly after that column's own due date D(c) - line 1b takes only payments made after the date at the top of the column. So each credited dollar's credit is strictly smaller than its own gross charge, and no dollar is credited to more than one column. The subtraction below is therefore floored at zero as an assertion, not as a correction.

Fact.Name: Penalty Worksheet line 14 — total penalty before the population gate
Fact.Description:
Penalty Worksheet line 14: "Add all amounts on lines 4, 7, 10, and 13 in all columns." The sum of the twelve printed cells, with the module's single HALF-UP Round applied here — this is the one figure that leaves the worksheet (onto Part III Section B line 19).
This fact is the raw worksheet arithmetic and is NOT the answer on its own: it computes a number for every filer whose Part I line 9 is evaluable, including filers whose estimated payments it cannot credit. /form2210Penalty below is the fact that decides whether this number may be claimed at all.

Fact.Name: The Penalty Worksheet's line 1b would carry an entry — the twelve Table 2 day counts are not exact
Fact.Description:
TRUE when at least one column has BOTH an underpayment on line 17 AND an estimated payment made after that column's own due date. That is exactly the condition under which the Penalty Worksheet's line 1b is non-empty, and therefore exactly the condition under which the twelve constant day counts this module reads off Table 2 stop being exact.
WHY THESE TWO TESTS ARE THE WHOLE CONDITION, not an approximation of it. Line 1b takes "the date and amount of each payment applied to the underpayment in the same column", capped by two printed limits: "Don't enter more than the underpayment amount on line 1a for each column", and "for each column, only enter payments you made or plan to make after the date at the top of the column". So a column's line 1b entry is bounded above by its own line 17 AND by the total of the payments made after its due date. Either bound at zero forces the entry to zero. When all four columns force it to zero, line 1b is empty, every underpayment "remained unpaid for an entire rate period", and Table 2's cells are the exact day counts rather than upper bounds.
WITHHOLDING IS NOT PART OF EITHER TEST, and that is printed rather than convenient: line 1b says "Do not enter any withheld federal income tax and excess social security or tier 1 RRTA on line 1b". A later quarter's withholding does satisfy an earlier column's underpayment on line 14 of Section A, but it never shortens that column's day count. So only the dated ESTIMATED payments can make this fact true.
WHAT HAPPENS WHEN IT IS TRUE — AND THIS PARAGRAPH IS NOT WHAT IT SAID WHEN IT SHIPPED. A prior version read: "/form2210Penalty resolves INCOMPLETE ... The remaining gap (/form2210PenaltyWorksheetLine1bDayCount) is a gap in the ENGINE rather than in the source: computing it needs, for each payment, the running total of the payments made before it, and this Fact Graph has no way to express a per-item aggregate over a collection that references the current item." THE FIRST HALF OF THAT IS NOW FALSE. The day counts ARE computed — see /form2210PenaltyWorksheetLine1bDayCount and the block note above it — so a return this fact reports true on is no longer refused for that reason.
THE ENGINE FINDING ITSELF SURVIVED AND ONLY THE INFERENCE FROM IT DID NOT. There is still no operator giving a collection item its own position, and a Filter's condition still binds to the filtered item, so S(i) genuinely cannot be computed from INSIDE item i. What did not follow is "therefore inexpressible": the payments are HOISTED to named slots by IndexOf with constant indices, and the recurrence is evaluated at module level against five band totals that were already on disk. No engine change was made or needed.
WHAT THIS FACT IS FOR NOW. It is the reason /form2210Penalty can compute a return whose dated payment list is LONGER than the sixteen hoisted slots: when this fact is false, every line 1b entry is empty, the credit is provably zero at any list length, and /form2210DatedPaymentsWithinSlotCapacity does not need to be consulted. /form2210Penalty reads the two inside one Any for exactly that reason.
FALSE ON EVERY RETURN THAT HAS NO DATED PAYMENTS, because all four "after this due date" pools are then a Complete zero. That is what makes this fact free of charge for the 519 returns whose penalty this dictionary already computes.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 line 19 — estimated tax penalty (Form 1040 line 38)
Fact.Description:
Form 2210 Part III Section B line 19, the underpayment penalty under IRC section 6654, carried to Form 1040 line 38. The section 6621 interest the Penalty Worksheet folds into its 0.07 multiplier is inside this figure.
FOUR OUTCOMES, AND THE LAST IS NOT A ZERO. The Switch below has no unconditional case, so a filer matching no arm resolves INCOMPLETE rather than $0: - $0 FIRST, and NOT as a no-penalty claim, when /form2210CombatZoneIrsFiguresPenalty is true: a filer with combat zone or contingency operation service who checks no Part II box leaves the penalty line blank and the IRS figures the penalty with the section 7508 postponement, which the computed arm does not apply. The $0 is the amount the return enters on line 38 (nothing), not a finding that nothing is owed. With no box, Form 2210 is not filed; with box A or box E alone, only page 1 is filed, so line 19 (page 2) is not part of the filed form. - $0 when estimatedPayments:/isExemptFromEstimatedTaxPenalty is true. This is a definite answer, not a default: it is the form's own "you don't owe a penalty" exit (the $1,000 de-minimis exits on lines 4 and 7, or the withholding safe harbor at line 9 vs line 6). - The Penalty Worksheet total (/form2210PenaltyWorksheetTotal) less the waiver the filer requests (/form2210Line19WaiverAmountApplied), when Part I line 9 is evaluable AND the dated estimated-payment detail reconciles to what the return reports AND the line 1b day-count credit is computable - either because line 1b is empty, or because the dated list fits the sixteen hoisted slots. That population INCLUDES returns whose line 1b carries entries. - INCOMPLETE otherwise, which is a refusal matching Form 2210's own default: the filer "aren't required to figure your penalty because the IRS will figure it and send you a bill for any unpaid amount". A zero penalty and an uncomputed penalty are different claims, and this fact never conflates them.
PLACEHOLDER ZERO IS A COMPLETENESS, NOT AN ARM. On a return whose /totalTax is itself PLACEHOLDER (an unfinished return the engine is still willing to give a provisional figure for), this fact resolves PLACEHOLDER 0.00: the exemption arm firing normally, with the engine propagating the provisional quality of estimatedPayments:/isExemptFromEstimatedTaxPenalty, which is likewise Placeholder on those returns. A consumer must gate on completeness, not only on value: reading Placeholder 0.00 as an authoritative $0 would put a settled zero on a return whose tax is not settled.
THE REFUSAL BOUNDARY is two facts about the DATA, not a fence on a question. First, estimatedPayments:/form2210DatedPaymentsReconcileEstimatedTax: the dated collection must add up to exactly what the return reports on Form 1040 line 26, or the detail is not a decomposition of it and cannot be used. A return that answers /paidEstimatedTaxesOrFromLastYear true with an annual amount and no dated collection therefore does not reconcile and stays Incomplete; a return with no estimated payments reconciles at zero-equals-zero. A filer whose only estimated payment was the 2024 overpayment applied on April 15, 2025 has an empty line 1b by construction and is computed. Second, the line 1b credit must be computable. /form2210PenaltyWorksheetLine1bDayCount computes it (the block note above it carries the derivation, and three printed worked examples pin it), so a filer with a payment made after a column's own due date is handed a number rather than a refusal. What is refused is a LIST LENGTH, not a shape: more than sixteen dated payments when the line 1b entries would be non-empty. The credit must be evaluated once per distinct payment date and only sixteen are addressable; i2210's own Table 1 grid holds six. /form2210DatedPaymentsWithinSlotCapacity carries that boundary and /form2210Line1bCreditWouldBeRequired short-circuits it when the credit is provably zero. It is a refusal by INCOMPLETENESS and not a knockout, because these returns file correctly and a knockout would block them: a coverage regression, not a guard.
WHY THE PRIOR-YEAR TAX IS AN INTAKE AND NOT A PRIOR-YEAR COMPUTATION. Line 8, and so line 9, rests on estimatedPayments:/form2210PriorYearTax, a taxpayer-attested writable, on the same footing as the Form 8396 carryforward-in. The graph never derives a prior-year figure, and nothing stops the taxpayer from stating one off their own 2024 return, which is what Form 2210 line 8 asks for in the first place.
DIRECTION: the computed figure is an UPPER BOUND on the true penalty - see the enumeration in the module note. The elections the filer does not make (Schedule AI, Part II box D) can only reduce it, and the inherited Part I approximations push it up.
WIRED TO FORM 1040 LINE 38: taxCalculations:/estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg carries this fact into /balanceDue and /finalTaxAmount, and taxCalculations:/form1040Line35aRefundAfterEstimatedTaxPenalty is the refund-side arm the module note's three-way routing needs.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II — the filer needs a separate Schedule SE as a per-period worksheet
Fact.Description:
TRUE when any filer on this return reported church employee income, which is the printed trigger for computing Schedule AI line 28 through a SEPARATE Schedule SE used as a per-period worksheet rather than through the ordinary 92.35%-of-net-profit route. The separate worksheet now computes in form2210SeparateScheduleSE.xml. This fact remains the route selector; missing or contradictory cumulative sources are refused by that module's substantiation verdict rather than by refusing every church-employee filer.
THE CONSERVATION RESERVE PROGRAM HALF OF THE PRINTED SENTENCE IS NOT GATED HERE, and the reason is the PERIOD dimension rather than the filer. scheduleSE /writableScheduleSeLine1bConservationReservePayments detects a CRP filer, but it is a single annual amount for the primary filer, and this gate would need the amount deducted in each cumulative period. Until a per-period CRP intake exists the half is disclosed rather than gated, here and in the section header, and such a filer takes the ordinary 92.35% route.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE, and the polarity is chosen rather than inherited: an UNANSWERED church employee income writable means the ordinary route applies, because that same writable is the only representation of church employee income the tree has — scheduleSE reaches the same reading from the same absence, so this gate cannot be stricter than the return it sits on.
A separate Schedule SE worksheet per Schedule AI period is required for the existing church-income route and for each activated CRP route. Per-filer annual deductible CRP now requires source allocation even if the annual SE tax is zero. The CRP worksheet uses distinct pre-deduction net profit and qualifying payment amounts and reconciles column D without double subtraction. Raw unqualified payments do not by themselves establish a deductible amount.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 28, primary filer, column (a) — net earnings from self-employment for 1/1/25-3/31/25
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION. Net earnings from self-employment for the cumulative period 1/1/25-3/31/25, for the primary filer's. This is a TIMING fact about the filer’s year that this graph does not hold: the tree knows the ANNUAL net earnings (scheduleSE line 6) and nothing about when in the year they were earned. The printed instruction tells the filer how to produce it — net profit for the period times 92.35% — so the multiplication is theirs, on their own per-period books.
Cumulative, not incremental: "Each period ... includes amounts from the previous period(s)". Column (d) is the whole year and is reconciled against scheduleSE line 6 by /form2210ScheduleAiPart2AttestationsConsistent, which also enforces the monotonicity that cumulative periods require.
NO DEPENDENCY BOUND HERE, DELIBERATELY. The obvious Limit — "at most the annual figure" — would put a Dependency inside a Writable, which the JS noCircularDeps check is structurally blind to and which can close a runtime cycle that gates green (the signature). The bound is expressed as a SINK consistency fact instead.
The sentence above is stale on its second clause: /form2210ScheduleAiPart2AttestationsConsistent does NOT enforce monotonicity over this line-28 series, and must not. That test was removed on purpose by the `FED-2210SE-MONOTONICITY-011` fix, because a CUMULATIVE NET series can lawfully decrease — Schedule SE line 4a prints the loss path ("If line 3 is more than zero, multiply line 3 by 92.35%. Otherwise, enter amount from line 3"; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sse.pdf, page 1) — and i2210's cumulative-period Note (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2210.pdf, page 8) says only that each period INCLUDES the previous ones, which is a statement about the time window and not about magnitude. /form2210ScheduleAiPart2AttestationsConsistentPrimary now says so in its own words ("THE LINE 28 SERIES CARRIES NO SUCH TEST, AND MUST NOT") and node-test form2210/schedule-ai-part2-line6-may-decrease-with-a-seasonal-loss pins the decrease as lawful. What column (d) IS still reconciled against is the annual figure; that half of the sentence stands. Do not restore the removed test from this paragraph. This legacy amount is already net earnings, NOT pre-CRP profit. If also answered while the new period CRP worksheet is active, its applied ordinary component must match that worksheet. It is not required on the new route and no CRP amount is subtracted from it.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 28 as entered, primary filer, column (a) — the $400 floor applied
Fact.Description:
Line 28 as it is actually ENTERED on the printed form: the attested net earnings for the period, or zero when they are under $400. "If your self-employment income for the applicable periods is less than $400, enter zero in Part II, line 28."
THE FLOOR IS COMPUTED, NOT ASKED. It is a pure function of the attested figure, so asking the filer to apply it would be asking them to do arithmetic the graph can do — the same boundary that keeps Schedule AI line 14 out of the attestation list. The comparison is STRICT ("less than $400"), so exactly $400 is entered in full, matching scheduleSE’s own line-4c treatment of the identical threshold.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 30, primary filer, column (a) — wages subject to social security tax for 1/1/25-3/31/25
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION. Actual wages for the cumulative period 1/1/25-3/31/25 that were subject to social security tax, for the primary filer's — including, per the printed exception, unreported tips from Form 4137 and wages from Form 8919 for the period.
This is the figure that consumes the prorated social security limit on line 29 before any self-employment earnings reach it. Column (d) reconciles against scheduleSE line 8d (/…SePriorSocialSecurityWages), which is exactly "wages plus Forms 4137 and 8919" — the same three components the printed line 30 and its exception name.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 31, primary filer, column (a)
Fact.Description: Line 31 = line 29 minus line 30, floored at zero: the part of column (a)’s prorated social security limit of $44025 that this filer’s wages have NOT already used. Line 29 is a printed per-column constant, stated inline here.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 33, primary filer, column (a) — the annualized social security portion
Fact.Description:
Line 33 = line 32 times the SMALLER of line 28 and line 31. Column (a)’s printed line-32 amount is 0.496, stated inline.
WHAT THE CONSTANT IS, so a TY2026 lift does not mistake it for a rate: 0.496 is the 12.4% social security rate carried through this column’s annualization, and it is taken from the PRINTED line rather than reconstructed — the form prints the product, so the form is what is quoted.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 35, primary filer, column (a) — the annualized Medicare portion
Fact.Description: Line 35 = line 28 times line 34. Column (a)’s printed line-34 amount is 0.116, stated inline. It is the 2.9% Medicare rate carried through this column’s annualization, quoted from the printed line rather than reconstructed. Unlike line 33 there is no limit to apply: the Medicare portion has no wage base.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 36, primary filer, column (a) — annualized SE tax for the period
Fact.Description:
Line 36 = line 33 + line 35, primary filer’s annualized self-employment tax for the cumulative period 1/1/25-3/31/25. Part I line 15 adds this to the other spouse’s line 36.
THE COMPUTED ARM FIRES ONLY WHEN the primary filer is known to be subject to self-employment tax; everything else falls through to a hard zero. That polarity is a decision, not an inherited shape. It buys two things. (i) It is the printed instruction: "If you had net earnings from self-employment during any period, complete Part II for that period" — a filer with no self-employment does not complete Part II, and their line 15 is zero. (ii) It keeps Part II from making every box-C return Incomplete: without it, a wage-only filer electing Schedule AI would have to answer eight per-period self-employment attestations that are all zero, and would resolve Incomplete until they did.
Annualized self-employment tax for this filer and cumulative period: add lines 33 and 35. A selected CRP worksheet uses period-specific earnings even when seasonal profit/loss makes annual SE tax zero. Outside that route, preserve the existing annual-subject compatibility gate. Unresolved selected CRP source data remain incomplete rather than silently contributing zero.

Column (d) reconciles against scheduleSE line 8d (/…SePriorSocialSecurityWages), which is exactly "wages plus Forms 4137 and 8919" — the same three components the printed line 30 and its exception name.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 31, secondary filer, column (d)
Fact.Description: Line 31 = line 29 minus line 30, floored at zero: the part of column (d)’s prorated social security limit of $176100 that this filer’s wages have NOT already used. Line 29 is a printed per-column constant, stated inline here.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 33, secondary filer, column (d) — the annualized social security portion
Fact.Description:
Line 33 = line 32 times the SMALLER of line 28 and line 31. Column (d)’s printed line-32 amount is 0.124, stated inline.
WHAT THE CONSTANT IS, so a TY2026 lift does not mistake it for a rate: 0.124 is the 12.4% social security rate carried through this column’s annualization, and it is taken from the PRINTED line rather than reconstructed — the form prints the product, so the form is what is quoted.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 35, secondary filer, column (d) — the annualized Medicare portion
Fact.Description: Line 35 = line 28 times line 34. Column (d)’s printed line-34 amount is 0.029, stated inline. It is the 2.9% Medicare rate carried through this column’s annualization, quoted from the printed line rather than reconstructed. Unlike line 33 there is no limit to apply: the Medicare portion has no wage base.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 36, secondary filer, column (d) — annualized SE tax for the period
Fact.Description:
Line 36 = line 33 + line 35, secondary filer’s annualized self-employment tax for the cumulative period 1/1/25-12/31/25. Part I line 15 adds this to the other spouse’s line 36.
THE COMPUTED ARM FIRES ONLY WHEN this is a joint return AND the secondary filer is known to be subject to self-employment tax — the MFJ conjunct because a separate Part II exists for a spouse only on a joint return; everything else falls through to a hard zero. That polarity is a decision, not an inherited shape. It buys two things. (i) It is the printed instruction: "If you had net earnings from self-employment during any period, complete Part II for that period" — a filer with no self-employment does not complete Part II, and their line 15 is zero. (ii) It keeps Part II from making every box-C return Incomplete: without it, a wage-only filer electing Schedule AI would have to answer eight per-period self-employment attestations that are all zero, and would resolve Incomplete until they did.
Annualized self-employment tax for this filer and cumulative period: add lines 33 and 35. A selected CRP worksheet uses period-specific earnings even when seasonal profit/loss makes annual SE tax zero. Outside that route, preserve the existing annual-subject compatibility gate. Unresolved selected CRP source data remain incomplete rather than silently contributing zero.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II — primary filer’s per-period attestations reconcile and are cumulative
Fact.Description:
The data fence over the primary filer’s eight Part II attestations, in the shape estimatedPayments /form2210DatedPaymentsReconcileEstimatedTax already ships: a fact ABOUT THE DATA, never a question put to the filer.
TWO CLAIMS, BOTH FROM THE PRINTED FORM. (i) RECONCILIATION — column (d) is the full year ("1/1/25-12/31/25"), so each series’ column (d) must equal the annual figure the tree already holds: line 28 against scheduleSE line 6 (the same line the church-employee instruction names as "net earnings from self-employment"), line 30 against scheduleSE line 8d (wages plus Forms 4137 and 8919, the three components the printed line 30 and its exception name). (ii) MONOTONICITY, ON THE WAGE SERIES ONLY — line 30 is wages subject to social security tax, and wages are nonnegative in every pay period, so a cumulative wage figure cannot run backwards and (a) ≤ (b) ≤ (c) ≤ (d) is a genuine contradiction test.
THE LINE 28 SERIES CARRIES NO SUCH TEST, AND MUST NOT. "Each period ... includes amounts from the previous period(s)" fixes the time WINDOW each column covers; it does not promise that the AMOUNT inside the window grows. Line 28 is net earnings, and Schedule SE prints the loss path on the very line the period figure is built from — "If line 3 is more than zero, multiply line 3 by 92.35% (0.9235). Otherwise, enter amount from line 3". A filer with $10,000 of net earnings through March and an $8,000 loss over April and May enters $9,235 in column (a) and $1,847 in column (b): lawful, arithmetically correct, and decreasing. The Min $0 limit on the underlying writable forbids a NEGATIVE entry; it does not forbid a DECREASE between two nonnegative ones. What this fence keeps over the line 28 series is column (d)’s reconciliation to the annual Schedule SE line 6, plus a PRESENCE read on each of columns (a), (b) and (c) — dropping the nondecreasing test without that read would have left the early columns unread, so a return answering column (d) alone would pass the fence and file with a silently unfigured penalty.
GATED ON THIS SPOUSE ACTUALLY HAVING A PART II, with the SAME polarity line 36 uses, and the reason is measured rather than assumed: the first shape of this fact conjoined both spouses unconditionally and resolved INCOMPLETE on a single filer’s return, because the secondary filer’s eight attestations are unanswered and always will be. A fence that is Incomplete on the population it is supposed to admit refuses everyone. So a spouse with no self-employment has nothing to reconcile and contributes TRUE.
THIS IS THE GRAPH’S ONLY LEVERAGE OVER AN ATTESTED ALLOCATION. The filer allocates income to periods and the graph cannot check the allocation itself — but it CAN check that the allocation adds up to the year it already knows, and that the WAGE series never runs backwards. A return failing either check is refused at Schedule AI line 27 rather than computed. The CRP worksheet also activates this annual reconciliation, including seasonal returns with zero annual SE tax but positive earnings in an earlier period. This prevents an annual-zero gate from ignoring period wage and source inputs.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II — the per-period attestations reconcile and are cumulative
Fact.Description:
The data fence over Part II’s sixteen attestations, in the shape estimatedPayments /form2210DatedPaymentsReconcileEstimatedTax already ships: a fact ABOUT THE DATA, never a question put to the filer.
TWO CLAIMS, BOTH FROM THE PRINTED FORM. (i) RECONCILIATION — column (d) is the full year ("1/1/25-12/31/25"), so each series’ column (d) must equal the annual figure the tree already holds: line 28 against scheduleSE line 6 (the same line the church-employee instruction names as "net earnings from self-employment"), line 30 against scheduleSE line 8d (wages plus Forms 4137 and 8919, the three components the printed line 30 and its exception name). (ii) MONOTONICITY, ON THE WAGE SERIES ONLY — line 30 is wages subject to social security tax, and wages are nonnegative in every pay period, so a cumulative wage figure cannot run backwards and (a) ≤ (b) ≤ (c) ≤ (d) is a genuine contradiction test.
THE LINE 28 SERIES CARRIES NO SUCH TEST, AND MUST NOT. "Each period ... includes amounts from the previous period(s)" fixes the time WINDOW each column covers; it does not promise that the AMOUNT inside the window grows. Otherwise, enter amount from line 3".
