The Min $0 limit on the underlying writable forbids a NEGATIVE entry; it does not forbid a DECREASE between two nonnegative ones. What the per-spouse facts keep over the line 28 series is column (d)’s reconciliation to the annual Schedule SE line 6, plus a PRESENCE read on each of columns (a), (b) and (c) — dropping the nondecreasing test without that read would have left the early columns unread, so a return answering column (d) alone would pass the fence and file with a silently unfigured penalty.
BOTH SPOUSES, EACH GATED ON HAVING A PART II AT ALL — the two per-spouse facts carry the claims and this one only conjoins them. A spouse with no self-employment contributes TRUE because they have nothing to reconcile.
THIS IS THE GRAPH’S ONLY LEVERAGE OVER AN ATTESTED ALLOCATION. The filer allocates income to periods and the graph cannot check the allocation itself — but it CAN check that the allocation adds up to the year it already knows, and that the WAGE series never runs backwards. A return failing either check is refused at Schedule AI line 27 rather than computed.
NOTE THE REACH: this fact is Incomplete whenever a spouse who HAS self-employment income leaves any of their eight attestations unanswered — which is exactly what makes an unanswered Part II refuse rather than quietly compute a zero. Consumers read it through Schedule AI line 27’s election gate, so a return that does NOT elect box C never evaluates it.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI line 14 — the ordinary rate schedule is EXACT for this return
Fact.Description:
The fence that makes a ladder-only line 14 admissible. TRUE only for the population where the ordinary rate schedule IS Form 1040 line 16 rather than an upper bound on it.
WHY AN UPPER BOUND IS NOT GOOD ENOUGH, read off the shipping tree rather than assumed: /qdcgLine25 is LesserOf(/qdcgLine23, /qdcgLine24) and /qdcgLine24 IS taxCalculations /ordinaryTaxOnTaxableIncome; /scheduleDTaxWorksheetTax is Round(LesserOf(/sdtwLine45, /sdtwLine46)) and /sdtwLine46 IS that same fact. So for both preferential worksheet populations the ordinary ladder is an upper bound — and an OVERSTATED line 14 walks through lines 17, 19, 21 and 27 into a line 27 that is too LARGE, i.e. wrong in the TAXPAYER’S DISFAVOUR. That is the exact category this module already refuses rather than approximates ("a number wrong in the TAXPAYER’S DISFAVOUR, which is not made acceptable by being ’safe’ in the World-#1 direction"). The Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet is worse still: it is a rate-stacking device whose line 6 EXCEEDS the ordinary tax, so the ladder does not even bound it.
THE LEGS, EACH ON A FACT THIS TREE ALREADY HOLDS: no qualified dividends and no net capital gain (the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet’s own entry amounts), no Schedule D Tax Worksheet and no Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet.
ALTERNATIVE MINIMUM TAX, FORM 4972 AND FORM 8814 ARE NOT LEGS. None of the three is tax on taxable income by the rate schedule: the alternative minimum tax is Schedule 2 line 2, and the Form 4972 and Form 8814 taxes are separate amounts added into Form 1040 line 16 beside the rate-schedule tax. The Schedule AI line 16 instruction names all three by name as line-16 contents, so a return carrying one of them still has an exact rate-schedule tax on line 13, and the tax itself reaches line 17 through the line 16 attestation, reconciled on column (d) by /form2210ScheduleAiPart1AttestationsConsistent.
SCHEDULE J HAS A LEG: scheduleJ /scheduleJApplies (complete-safe) makes this fence FALSE, and the same leg sits in the four /form2210ScheduleAiPreferentialCharacterInputsCompleteCol* facts, so a Schedule J return takes neither line 14 route. Line 14 stays Incomplete and /form2210ScheduleAiElectedButUnsubstantiated blocks a box C election rather than filing a line 14 figured without the income averaging the annual return used. SECTION 1062(a) is detected through the Schedule 3 line 13z label 1062NL and refused by /knockoutForm2210Section1062aElectionNotBuilt when a penalty results. FORM 8615 IS NOT. What is unrepresented there is the COMPUTATION — the child’s tax at the parent’s rate — which is all the scope ledger’s Form 2555 row claims when it says "Form 8615 is unreachable for want of any representation rather than refused" about that worksheet’s line 4. The FILER is entirely representable: a child who can be claimed as a dependent is /filers/*/canBeClaimed, and the unearned income that triggers section 1(g) arrives through the interest and dividend collections this dictionary already carries. So such a return can be ENTERED today and this fence simply does not ask — a missing intake, not a representability wall. The OTHER half of the same section 1(g) regime, the parental election on Form 8814, is not a leg either, for the opposite reason: its tax is fully computed (form8814 /form8814TotalTax) and belongs on Schedule AI line 16, not line 14. Until an intake exists the Form 8615 population would reach this fence looking like an ordinary-ladder return, but form8615 /mustFileForm8615 is a member of flow /flowIsKnockedOut, so such a return is blocked from submission long before Schedule AI is reached. What remains true is that this fence does not ASK, so it is the knockout and not this fact that carries the population.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE, and the polarity is the conservative one CHOSEN rather than inherited: if any leg is Incomplete the fence cannot be shown to hold, so it does not hold, and the exact ordinary ladder is not taken.
WHAT THIS FACT DECIDES. It decides ONE route: whether line 14 may take the exact ordinary ladder on a column that answers no character input. It no longer decides whether the schedule as a whole is substantiated. Line 27 in all four columns and /form2210ScheduleAiElectedButUnsubstantiated read /form2210ScheduleAiLine14SubstantiatedForEveryColumn instead, because this fact reads the ANNUAL preferential figures and is therefore permanently FALSE for a box C filer with qualified dividends or a net capital gain, whose line 14 the period-specific worksheets now compute. The sentences this replaces said the return is refused at line 14 when the fence fails, and that a large capital gain late in the year is precisely this fence’s exclusion. Both were true only while the ordinary ladder was the only route.
WHAT THE SCHEDULE STILL TURNS AWAY, named plainly: i2210 opens the Schedule AI instructions with two archetypes, "you operated your business on a seasonal basis or had a large capital gain late in the year". The FIRST is fully served. The SECOND is served too once the period character amounts are answered, and refused when they are not. The Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet remains excluded on both routes.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 7 — the standard deduction, the same figure in every column
Fact.Description:
Line 7: "In each column, enter the amount of your standard deduction from Form 1040 or 1040-SR." ONE fact rather than four, because the printed line says "in each column" and the standard deduction does not vary by period — it is an annual figure the filer gets in full whatever the timing of their income.
The printed Form 1040-NR exception ("enter -0-") and the Indian students and business apprentices exception do not apply: this dictionary files Form 1040 / 1040-SR returns.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 1, column (a) — adjusted gross income for 1/1/25-3/31/25
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION. Adjusted gross income for the cumulative period 1/1/25-3/31/25. The graph holds the ANNUAL AGI and nothing about when in the year it arose, and that timing is the whole subject of this schedule — so the filer allocates, and the graph RECONCILES: column (d) is the full year and must equal /agi, which /form2210ScheduleAiPart1AttestationsConsistent enforces along with the monotonicity the cumulative periods require.
No Dependency bound is placed on this Writable, deliberately — see the same note on Part II’s line 28.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 3, column (a) — annualized income
Fact.Description: Line 3 = line 1 times line 2. Column (a)’s printed annualization amount is 4, stated inline: it is the reciprocal of the fraction of the year the period covers, so a period’s income is scaled to what a full year at that rate would be.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 4, column (a) — itemized deductions for 1/1/25-3/31/25
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION. Itemized deductions for the cumulative period 1/1/25-3/31/25. The printed line carries its own default for everyone else: "If you itemize, enter itemized deductions for the period shown in each column. All others, enter -0-, and skip to line 7." A filer taking the standard deduction answers zero here and line 8 picks up line 7.
Column (d) reconciles against scheduleA /totalItemizedDeductions when the return claims itemized deductions, and against zero when it does not — both legs are in /form2210ScheduleAiPart1AttestationsConsistent.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 6, column (a) — annualized itemized deductions
Fact.Description: Line 6 = line 4 times line 5. Line 5 prints the SAME annualization amounts as line 2 (4 in column (a)) — the deductions are scaled to a full year exactly as the income on line 3 is.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 8, column (a) — the larger of annualized itemized or standard
Fact.Description: Line 8: "Enter the larger of line 6 or line 7." The annualized itemized deductions for the period against the standard deduction — the same larger-of choice the annual return makes, taken separately in each column because annualizing a partial year’s itemized deductions can put a filer on either side of it.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 9, column (a) — qualified business income deduction for 1/1/25-3/31/25
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION. The deduction for qualified business income attributable to the cumulative period 1/1/25-3/31/25. NOT annualized — the printed schedule multiplies lines 1 and 4 by the annualization amounts and does not multiply line 9, so it enters line 10 at face value.
WHY THIS IS ATTESTED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED TO ZERO. A zero default here would raise line 13, raise line 14 and RAISE the penalty — "safe" in direction, but wrong in the taxpayer’s disfavour, which this module refuses rather than approximates. Column (d) reconciles against taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 10, column (a)
Fact.Description: Line 10 = lines 8 + 9, the total deduction against this column’s annualized income. NOTE THE NUMBERING TRAP: this is SCHEDULE AI line 10, "Add lines 8 and 9" — not Form 2210 Part III line 10, the required installment, which is what Schedule AI line 27 feeds. The two are different lines on different parts of the same form.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 11, column (a)
Fact.Description: Line 11 = line 3 minus line 10: this column’s annualized income after the deduction. Not floored here — the printed floor sits on line 13.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 13, column (a) — annualized taxable income
Fact.Description:
Line 13 = line 11 minus line 12, floored at zero. LINE 12 IS THE PRINTED -0- for Form 1040, 1040-SR and 1040-NR filers ("enter -0- in each column"), which is every return this dictionary files, so the subtraction is stated as the floor alone rather than given a fact of its own — a fact whose only possible value is zero and whose only reader is this line would be a computed fact nothing meaningfully reads.
This is the amount line 14 computes the tax on.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 13, column (a) — at the Tax Table's own midpoint
Fact.Description:
Line 13 moved onto the Tax Table’s bracket midpoints, which is what line 14’s printed instruction requires: "see the instructions for your tax return for the applicable Tax Table or worksheet to use", and the Tax Table is a table of $50 bands (smaller at the bottom) whose tax is computed at the band’s MIDPOINT rather than at the exact figure. Above $100,000 the Tax Computation Worksheet applies instead and the exact amount is used.
THIS MIRRORS taxCalculations /roundedTaxableIncome CASE FOR CASE, on this column’s line 13 instead of on the annual taxable income, and it has to be a separate fact for the same reason line 14 does: the Fact Graph has no function abstraction, so a derivation cannot be evaluated at a different input. Keeping the two in step matters — a Schedule AI column that skipped the midpoint convention would disagree with the annual return on column (d), where the two compute the same quantity.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 14, column (a) — the tax on annualized taxable income
Fact.Description: Line 14: "Figure your tax on the amount on line 13. See instructions." For column (a), this line uses the period-specific Schedule D Tax Worksheet when its supported route is selected; otherwise it uses the period-specific Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet when all character inputs are answered. Both copies compute tax on this column’s line 13 using the six cumulative annualized character inputs stored in form2210. The exact ordinary ladder remains the fallback only when all six character inputs for this column are unanswered and the existing exactness fence is satisfied. Partial, inconsistent, or unsupported answered inputs do not fall through to ordinary tax. This preserves today’s default behavior and never treats a missing character amount as zero. The copies intentionally do not model the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet, Schedule J, Form 8615, or a section 1062(a) adjustment; their existing boundaries remain in force. Alternative minimum tax and the Form 4972 and Form 8814 taxes are not part of this line: they are not tax on line 13 by the rate schedule or a worksheet, and the line 16 instruction carries them (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2210.pdf, page 10). The applicable worksheet routes are listed at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2210.pdf, page 10.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 15, column (a) — self-employment tax from Part II
Fact.Description:
Line 15: "Self-employment tax from line 36 (complete Part II below)". On a joint return this is the SUM of both spouses’ line 36, which the instructions state in the direction the printed line only implies: "Enter on line 15 of Schedule AI, Part I, the combined amounts from line 36 of each spouse’s Part II."
This is the only place Part I reads Part II, which is why unit 3 could land first.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 16, column (a) — other taxes for 1/1/25-3/31/25
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION. Other taxes owed because of events in the cumulative period 1/1/25-3/31/25, including Additional Medicare Tax and Net Investment Income Tax.
THIS IS THE ONE SERIES WHOSE ZERO DEFAULT WOULD BE DANGEROUS, which is why it is a REQUIRED attestation rather than a defaulted writable. Run the direction: line 16 defaulted to zero lowers line 17, lowers line 19, lowers line 21, lowers line 27, lowers Part III line 10 and lowers the PENALTY. Every other attestation on this schedule errs the other way. Nothing about Schedule AI’s never-exceeds-the-regular-method bound rescues it either: that bound says Schedule AI never demands MORE than the regular method, and an understated line 16 pushes the filer further BELOW it than the form allows.
So it is unanswerable-by-default on purpose: leaving it blank makes this column Incomplete and refuses the return rather than quietly understating the penalty. Column (d) reconciles against the Schedule 2 lines i2210’s Part I line-2 table names — lines 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17a, 17c through 17j, 17l, 17z and 19 as this dictionary models them — plus any alternative minimum tax, the Form 4972 tax and the Form 8814 tax, and WITHOUT self-employment tax, which Schedule AI line 15 carries on its own printed line. The full derivation from print lives on /form2210ScheduleAiPart1AttestationsConsistent, which is the fact that enforces it.
THE THREE TAXES THE INSTRUCTION NAMES OUTSIDE THE PART I LINE 2 TABLE, and how each is figured for a period. Alternative minimum tax: figure alternative minimum taxable income from the income and deductions of the period, multiply it by the period's annualization amount (line 2) before subtracting the exemption, and enter the resulting AMT. The Form 4972 tax on a lump-sum distribution and the Form 8814 tax on a child's interest and dividends are taxes owed because of an event, and enter in the column whose months include that event (the distribution, or the child's income), carried into every later column because the periods are cumulative. The graph does not refigure these per period: like the Net Investment Income Tax on this line and the annualized credits on line 18, the filer figures them and the graph holds the full-year column to the annual return.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 17, column (a) — total tax
Fact.Description: Line 17 = lines 14 + 15 + 16: this column’s total annualized tax before credits.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 18, column (a) — credits for 1/1/25-3/31/25
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION. The credits allowable for the cumulative period 1/1/25-3/31/25 — "the same type of credits as allowed on Form 2210, Part I, lines 1 and 3", i.e. the nonrefundable credits that reduced the tax on Part I line 1 and the refundable credits on Part I line 3.
THE PRINTED INSTRUCTION ASKS THE FILER TO ANNUALIZE INSIDE THE CREDIT, not to prorate the credit: "When figuring your credits, annualize any item of income or deduction used to figure each credit. For example, if your earned income (and AGI) for the first period (column (a)) is $8,000 and you qualify for the earned income credit (EIC), use your annualized earned income ($32,000) to figure your EIC for column (a)." That is a recomputation of each credit at annualized inputs, which is why this is attested rather than derived from the annual credit — the graph cannot re-run every credit chain at four hypothetical income levels.
Column (d) reconciles against the annual credits the tree holds: taxCalculations /nonRefundableCredits (Form 1040 line 21, Form 2210 Part I line 1’s credits) plus /totalOtherPaymentsRefundableCredits (Form 1040 line 32, Part I line 3).

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 19, column (a)
Fact.Description: Line 19 = line 17 minus line 18, floored at zero: this column’s annualized tax after credits.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 21, column (a) — the applicable percentage applied
Fact.Description:
Line 21 = line 19 times line 20. Column (a)’s printed applicable percentage is 22.5%, stated inline.
WHAT THE PERCENTAGE IS DOING: it is the same 90%-of-current-year-tax safe harbour the regular method applies annually (Form 2210 Part I line 5), prorated across the four cumulative periods — 22.5% is a quarter of 90%, 45% is half, 67.5% is three quarters and 90% is the whole. So a filer who has earned a quarter of the year’s income by 3/31 owes a quarter of the year’s safe-harbour demand, which is the entire point of the schedule.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 1, column (b) — adjusted gross income for 1/1/25-5/31/25
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION. Adjusted gross income for the cumulative period 1/1/25-5/31/25. The graph holds the ANNUAL AGI and nothing about when in the year it arose, and that timing is the whole subject of this schedule — so the filer allocates, and the graph RECONCILES: column (d) is the full year and must equal /agi, which /form2210ScheduleAiPart1AttestationsConsistent enforces along with the monotonicity the cumulative periods require.
No Dependency bound is placed on this Writable, deliberately — see the same note on Part II’s line 28.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 3, column (b) — annualized income
Fact.Description: Line 3 = line 1 times line 2. Column (b)’s printed annualization amount is 2.4, stated inline: it is the reciprocal of the fraction of the year the period covers, so a period’s income is scaled to what a full year at that rate would be.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 4, column (b) — itemized deductions for 1/1/25-5/31/25
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION. Itemized deductions for the cumulative period 1/1/25-5/31/25. The printed line carries its own default for everyone else: "If you itemize, enter itemized deductions for the period shown in each column. All others, enter -0-, and skip to line 7." Fact.Name: Schedule AI line 14 reached a tax by a supported route in all four columns
Fact.Description:
TRUE when line 14 resolves in columns (a), (b), (c) and (d) — that is, when every column reached a tax by a route this dictionary computes. Two routes reach it: the period-specific Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet or Schedule D Tax Worksheet copy, taken when that column's six character inputs are all answered and none of the unsupported quantities is present; and the exact ordinary ladder, taken when that column answers no character input at all and /form2210ScheduleAiExactLadderFenceSatisfied holds.
WHY THIS REPLACED THE BARE EXACT-LADDER FENCE at Schedule AI line 27 in all four columns and at /form2210ScheduleAiElectedButUnsubstantiated. The fence asks whether the ordinary ladder is the whole story on this return, and until the per-period preferential worksheets existed that was the same question as whether line 14 can be computed. It is no longer. The instructions for line 14 name the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet and the Schedule D Tax Worksheet among the routes to use, and both are now computed per period. A filer who elects box C, holds qualified dividends or a net capital gain, and answers the period character amounts therefore has a line 14 in every column, while the fence stays FALSE — permanently, because the fence reads the ANNUAL qualified dividend and capital gain figures, which are exactly what that filer has. Gating on the fence refused that return twice over: line 27 went Incomplete in all four columns, so /form2210Penalty could not compute and the Form 1040 line 38 estimated-tax leg fell to a hard zero, AND the submission guard blocked the return outright, forcing the filer off the annualized method and onto the regular one, which is the higher figure whenever Schedule AI would have helped at all. Neither refusal had authority behind it once the worksheets shipped.
THE CORRECTNESS PROOF THAT MAKES ADMISSION SAFE rather than a silent under-charge is column (d). Column (d) is the full year at annualization factor 1, so its worksheet copy must reproduce the annual worksheet exactly. It does, to the cent: node-test form2210/schedule-ai-elected-period-qdcg-worksheets-substantiate-the-election pins /form2210ScheduleAiLine14ColD and preferentialRateTax /qdcgLine25 at the same 9,390.85 on one return.
WHAT IT STILL TURNS AWAY. The Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet is read by /form2210ScheduleAiPreferentialCharacterInputsCompleteColA and its three siblings, and keeps every column that needs it off the preferential route; with no character input answered it keeps the exact ladder shut as well, through the fence, which reads the same quantity. Alternative minimum tax and the Form 4972 and Form 8814 taxes are NOT turned away: they are not tax on line 13, and they reach line 17 through the line 16 attestation. Schedule J and Form 8615 stay disclosures rather than gates, for the reasons /form2210ScheduleAiExactLadderFenceSatisfied records; a Form 8615 child is in any case knocked out of this flow before Schedule AI is reached. A column with PARTIAL character inputs, and a column whose answered amounts contradict the full-year return, both leave line 14 Incomplete and this fact FALSE — the fail-closed direction. Witnessed separately, because the two are different failures: form2210/schedule-ai-line14-period-d-full-year-character-mismatch answers one of column (d) six amounts and no more, and form2210/schedule-ai-elected-column-d-character-mismatch-fails-closed-and-blocks answers all six but sets column (d) qualified dividends one dollar above the annual figure, which the column (d) gate reconciles against the return itself. A third case, form2210/schedule-ai-elected-early-column-partial-inputs-fails-closed-and-blocks, holds the same for a column that is not column (d) and has no annual figure to reconcile against. Note that form2210/schedule-ai-line14-period-mixed-input-fallback is NOT one of these: it answers column (a) completely and the other three not at all, so every column reaches a tax — column (a) by the worksheet copy and the rest by the exact ladder — and this fact is TRUE there. That case is the witness that the two routes coexist on one return.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE, and it has to be: each conjunct is an IsComplete, so an unanswered or refused column makes this Complete false rather than Incomplete, which is what a submission guard needs in order to fire at all. On every return that does not elect Schedule AI this fact is still evaluated but nothing reads it except line 27, whose own switch is already behind the election.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 15, column (d) — self-employment tax from Part II
Fact.Description:
Line 15: "Self-employment tax from line 36 (complete Part II below)". On a joint return this is the SUM of both spouses’ line 36, which the instructions state in the direction the printed line only implies: "Enter on line 15 of Schedule AI, Part I, the combined amounts from line 36 of each spouse’s Part II."
This is the only place Part I reads Part II, which is why unit 3 could land first.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 16, column (d) — other taxes for 1/1/25-12/31/25
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION. Other taxes owed because of events in the cumulative period 1/1/25-12/31/25, including Additional Medicare Tax and Net Investment Income Tax.
THIS IS THE ONE SERIES WHOSE ZERO DEFAULT WOULD BE DANGEROUS, which is why it is a REQUIRED attestation rather than a defaulted writable. Run the direction: line 16 defaulted to zero lowers line 17, lowers line 19, lowers line 21, lowers line 27, lowers Part III line 10 and lowers the PENALTY. Every other attestation on this schedule errs the other way. Nothing about Schedule AI’s never-exceeds-the-regular-method bound rescues it either: that bound says Schedule AI never demands MORE than the regular method, and an understated line 16 pushes the filer further BELOW it than the form allows.
So it is unanswerable-by-default on purpose: leaving it blank makes this column Incomplete and refuses the return rather than quietly understating the penalty. Column (d) reconciles against the Schedule 2 lines i2210’s Part I line-2 table names — lines 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17a, 17c through 17j, 17l, 17z and 19 as this dictionary models them — plus any alternative minimum tax, the Form 4972 tax and the Form 8814 tax, and WITHOUT self-employment tax, which Schedule AI line 15 carries on its own printed line. The full derivation from print lives on /form2210ScheduleAiPart1AttestationsConsistent, which is the fact that enforces it.
THE THREE TAXES THE INSTRUCTION NAMES OUTSIDE THE PART I LINE 2 TABLE, and how each is figured for a period. Alternative minimum tax: figure alternative minimum taxable income from the income and deductions of the period, multiply it by the period's annualization amount (line 2) before subtracting the exemption, and enter the resulting AMT. The Form 4972 tax on a lump-sum distribution and the Form 8814 tax on a child's interest and dividends are taxes owed because of an event, and enter in the column whose months include that event (the distribution, or the child's income), carried into every later column because the periods are cumulative. The graph does not refigure these per period: like the Net Investment Income Tax on this line and the annualized credits on line 18, the filer figures them and the graph holds the full-year column to the annual return.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 17, column (d) — total tax
Fact.Description: Line 17 = lines 14 + 15 + 16: this column’s total annualized tax before credits.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 18, column (d) — credits for 1/1/25-12/31/25
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION. The credits allowable for the cumulative period 1/1/25-12/31/25 — "the same type of credits as allowed on Form 2210, Part I, lines 1 and 3", i.e. the nonrefundable credits that reduced the tax on Part I line 1 and the refundable credits on Part I line 3.
THE PRINTED INSTRUCTION ASKS THE FILER TO ANNUALIZE INSIDE THE CREDIT, not to prorate the credit: "When figuring your credits, annualize any item of income or deduction used to figure each credit. For example, if your earned income (and AGI) for the first period (column (a)) is $8,000 and you qualify for the earned income credit (EIC), use your annualized earned income ($32,000) to figure your EIC for column (a)." That is a recomputation of each credit at annualized inputs, which is why this is attested rather than derived from the annual credit — the graph cannot re-run every credit chain at four hypothetical income levels.
Column (d) reconciles against the annual credits the tree holds: taxCalculations /nonRefundableCredits (Form 1040 line 21, Form 2210 Part I line 1’s credits) plus /totalOtherPaymentsRefundableCredits (Form 1040 line 32, Part I line 3).

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 19, column (d)
Fact.Description: Line 19 = line 17 minus line 18, floored at zero: this column’s annualized tax after credits.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 21, column (d) — the applicable percentage applied
Fact.Description:
Line 21 = line 19 times line 20. Column (d)’s printed applicable percentage is 90%, stated inline.
WHAT THE PERCENTAGE IS DOING: it is the same 90%-of-current-year-tax safe harbour the regular method applies annually (Form 2210 Part I line 5), prorated across the four cumulative periods — 22.5% is a quarter of 90%, 45% is half, 67.5% is three quarters and 90% is the whole. So a filer who has earned a quarter of the year’s income by 3/31 owes a quarter of the year’s safe-harbour demand, which is the entire point of the schedule.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I — the per-period attestations reconcile and are cumulative
Fact.Description:
The data fence over Part I’s twenty attestations, in the shape estimatedPayments /form2210DatedPaymentsReconcileEstimatedTax already ships: a fact ABOUT THE DATA, never a question put to the filer.
RECONCILIATION — column (d) is the full year ("1/1/25-12/31/25"), so each series’ column (d) must equal the annual figure the tree already holds: line 1 against /agi line 4 against scheduleA /totalItemizedDeductions when the return claims itemized deductions, and against ZERO when it does not — the printed line’s own "All others, enter -0-" line 9 against taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction line 16 against the Schedule 2 lines i2210’s OWN Part I line-2 table names, less self-employment tax, plus AMT and the Form 4972 and Form 8814 taxes — see the derivation below line 18 against taxCalculations /nonRefundableCredits plus /totalOtherPaymentsRefundableCredits, the Form 1040 line 21 and line 32 totals that are Form 2210 Part I lines 1 and 3 MONOTONICITY — "Each period ... includes amounts from the previous period(s)", so (a) ≤ (b) ≤ (c) ≤ (d) in all five series.
THIS IS THE GRAPH’S ONLY LEVERAGE OVER AN ATTESTED ALLOCATION, and it is real leverage: the filer decides how income falls across the periods and the graph cannot audit that, but it CAN insist the allocation adds up to the year it already knows and never runs backwards. A return failing either check is refused at line 27 rather than computed.
INCOMPLETE WHEN ANY ATTESTATION IS UNANSWERED, which is what makes an incomplete Schedule AI refuse rather than compute on defaults. Consumers read it through line 27’s election gate, so a return that does not elect box C never evaluates it.
================ WHERE LINE 16’s TARGET COMES FROM, derived from print ================
THE PRINTED RULE, in full: "Enter all of the other taxes you owed because of events that occurred during the months shown in the column headings. Include the same taxes used to figure Form 2210, Part I, line 2 (except self-employment tax), plus the tax from Form 4972 ...; Form 8814 ...; and any alternative minimum tax (AMT)."
FORM 2210 PART I LINE 2 IS NOT SCHEDULE 2 LINE 21, and that is the whole correction. Its caption reads like Form 1040 line 23 ("Other taxes, including self-employment tax and, if applicable, Additional Medicare Tax and/or Net Investment Income Tax"), but i2210 defines it with an EXPLICIT TABLE of Schedule 2 lines: "Line 4, Line 8 (additional tax on distributions only), Line 9,* Line 11, Line 12, Line 14, Line 15, Line 16, Line 17a, Line 17c, Line 17d, Line 17e, Line 17f, Line 17g, Line 17h, Line 17i, Line 17j, Line 17l, Line 17z, and Line 19." That list is a SUBSET of Schedule 2 line 21 — a fact estimatedPayments already records on /form2210Line4CurrentYearTax ("the 2210 line-2 other taxes base is a SUBSET of Schedule 2").
THE TEN ADDENDS OF taxCalculations /line21OfSchedule2, each accepted or rejected by its printed Schedule 2 line number against that table: line 4 scheduleSE /selfEmploymentTax IN the table, then REMOVED by line 16’s own "(except self-employment tax)" — and it is not lost, Schedule AI line 15 carries the annualized SE tax on its own printed line line 5 form4137 (unreported tip income) NOT IN THE TABLE line 6 form8919 (uncollected tax on wages) NOT IN THE TABLE line 8 form5329 /form5329AdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions IN, and the table’s qualifier "(additional tax on distributions only)" is exactly this fact line 9 scheduleH /scheduleHTotalHouseholdEmploymentTaxes IN (see the footnote below) line 11 form8959 /additionalMedicareTax IN line 12 form8960 /netInvestmentIncomeTax IN line 13 formW2s /schedule2Line13UncollectedBox12Tax NOT IN THE TABLE line 17c hsa /hsaCollectionRouteAdditionalTax20PctTotal IN (the only shipping leg of that printed line since a prior step retired the top-level scalar route form8889 /form8889AdditionalTax20Pct) ═══ THE FULL FOURTEEN-ADDEND LIST ═══ THE TEN-ADDEND LIST ABOVE IS KEPT AS WRITTEN AND IS STALE. taxCalculations /line21OfSchedule2 carries FOURTEEN addends at this unit's base; five arrived after the list was written and were unclassified here, which is exactly the drift three hsa units named for the lead rather than made. The full fourteen, re-derived line by line against the printed table (2025 Instructions for Form 2210, "Line 2", the "IF you file for 2025... 1040, 1040-NR, or 1040-SR / Schedule 2 (Form 1040)" row; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2210.pdf, page 2, the RIGHT-hand column of page 2 — the left-hand column of those same extracted lines is the waiver-request prose and belongs to nothing here): line 4 scheduleSE /selfEmploymentTax IN the table, then REMOVED by line 16's own "(except self-employment tax)" line 5 form4137 NOT IN THE TABLE line 6 form8919 NOT IN THE TABLE line 8 form5329 /form5329AdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions IN — the table's qualifier "(additional tax on distributions only)" is exactly this fact line 8 hsa /hsaExcessContributionExciseTaxForm5329PartVii OUT. Form 5329 Part VII is the 6% excise on excess HSA CONTRIBUTIONS. It prints on the same Schedule 2 line 8, but the table admits that line ONLY as "Line 8 (additional tax on distributions only)", and an excise on a contribution is not a tax on a distribution line 8 hsa /archerMsaExcessContributionExciseTaxForm5329PartVi OUT, for the identical reason: Form 5329 Part VI is the 6% excise on excess Archer MSA CONTRIBUTIONS line 9 scheduleH /scheduleHTotalHouseholdEmploymentTaxes IN (footnote below) line 11 form8959 /additionalMedicareTax IN line 12 form8960 /netInvestmentIncomeTax IN line 13 formW2s /schedule2Line13UncollectedBox12Tax NOT IN THE TABLE line 17c hsa /hsaCollectionRouteAdditionalTax20PctTotal IN line 17d hsa /hsaTestingPeriodFailureAdditionalTax IN, the table prints "Line 17d," — WIRED by this unit line 17e hsa /archerMsaSchedule2Line17eAdditional20PctTax IN, the table prints "Line 17e," — WIRED by this unit line 17f hsa /medicareAdvantageMsaSchedule2Line17fAdditional50PctTax IN, the table prints "Line 17f," — WIRED by this unit line 17k formW2s /schedule2Line17kGoldenParachutePaymentsTax NOT IN THE TABLE THE TABLE ALSO NAMES lines 14, 15, 16, 17a, 17g, 17h, 17i, 17j, 17l, 17z and 19, and each is in the Add: schedule2 carries a complete-safe fact for every one of them (line 17z as its three legs, the filer's entry, the HSA pledge tax and the negative Form 8978 adjustment; line 19 as form4255 /form4255NetEpeRecaptureFromLine1dOrZero), the same facts estimatedPayments /form2210PartILine2OtherTaxes adds for Part I line 2. A box-C filer who owes one of them and attests line 16 including it is admitted. EVERY WIRED ADDEND IS COMPLETE-SAFE $0 OFF ITS POPULATION, read out of its own body rather than assumed, so the Add's completeness is unchanged on every return that answers none of them and the Equal's verdict is unchanged there too. ONE NAMING GAP, stated rather than silently fixed: the hsa records paragraphs that reported this drift call the carrier "/form2210Line2OtherTaxes". No such fact has ever existed in this module. The Schedule 2 mirror they mean is this Equal, on /form2210ScheduleAiPart1AttestationsConsistent. The same correction applies to this Description's own reference above to "estimatedPayments ... /form2210Line4CurrentYearTax": the fact that carries the "SUBSET of Schedule 2" note is estimatedPayments:/form2210CurrentYearTax, and the note is an authority comment on it. The note's substance is unchanged by this landing and stands.
Schedule 2 line 1z is not in the table either, at any of its parts, so the excess advance premium tax credit repayment and the clean-vehicle dealer-transfer repayments do not belong here. Schedule 2 line 17k, golden parachute payments (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s2.pdf, page 2, "Golden parachute payments"), is NOT IN THE TABLE either: the table goes from line 17j straight to line 17l (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2210.pdf, page 2, "Line 17j, Line 17l,"), so a line 17k tax is part of Schedule 2 line 21 but does not belong in Schedule AI line 16's target. AMT is Schedule 2 LINE 2, also outside the table, which is why the printed line-16 rule has to name it separately — and that separate naming is the strongest internal evidence that the table, not Schedule 2 line 21, is the base being described. Form 4972 and Form 8814 are named for the same reason from the other side: those taxes sit on FORM 1040 line 16, not on Schedule 2 at all, so Schedule AI line 14’s rate-schedule tax does not pick them up. Both are in the target: form1099RFrontier /form4972TaxTotal (Form 4972 line 30) and form8814 /form8814TotalTax (Form 8814 line 15 over every elected child), each Complete $0 on a return that has neither, so the target is unchanged there.
WHAT THIS REPLACED, kept as record because the measurement behind it is true. The contract prescribed "/totalAdditionalTaxesOwed LESS the self-employment tax", reading the printed exception as a subtraction to perform here; the church-employee witness measured that target going NEGATIVE (0.00 less 707.00 on a return with self-employment income), refusing every correctly attested seasonal-business filer. The subtraction was dropped and /totalAdditionalTaxesOwed (Schedule 2 line 3) plus Form 8959 plus Form 8960 shipped instead. That target is still wrong in BOTH directions, which is what this landing fixes. TOO LOW: it omitted four modeled addends the table names — Schedule 2 line 8, line 9, and line 17c on both its shipping legs — so a filer with any of those taxes who attested line 16 correctly was REFUSED. TOO HIGH: reading Schedule 2 line 3 rather than line 2 for the AMT dragged line 1z in with it, and the table names no part of line 1z, so a filer with an excess advance premium tax credit repayment or a clean-vehicle dealer-transfer repayment was refused for the opposite reason. The review that raised this counted six omitted terms by taking Part I line 2 to be Schedule 2 line 21; the table makes it four, because lines 5, 6 and 13 are not in it.
WHY PRINT-EXACT HERE WHEN Part I line 4 KEEPS A DELIBERATE OVERSTATEMENT. Line 4’s approximation is one-sided-safe: it only ever fails to exempt, never falsely exempts. An EQUAL fence has no safe direction at all. Overstate the target and a correctly attesting filer is refused (the church-employee bug); understate it and an understated attestation is admitted, which lowers line 17, line 19, line 21, line 27, Part III line 10 and the PENALTY. So the target has to be the printed one, and consistency with line 4’s bound is not a reason to keep an inexact one.
THE SCHEDULE H FOOTNOTE IS APPLIED THROUGH PART I LINE 2. The table's asterisk on line 9 reads: "Don't include household employment taxes if both of the following are true: (1) you didn't have federal income tax withheld from your income, and (2) you wouldn't be required to make estimated tax payments even if the household employment taxes weren't included" (IRC 3510(b)(2)). The target reads line 9 as estimatedPayments /form2210HouseholdEmploymentTaxesOnLine2, the same household employment taxes Part I line 2 adds: the full Schedule H line 26 amount, or zero when both conditions hold. Line 16 takes "the same taxes used to figure Form 2210, Part I, line 2", so the two always agree.
THE AMT, FORM 4972 AND FORM 8814 TERMS ARE LIVE. Neither line 14 route turns these returns away, so a box C filer with alternative minimum tax, a Form 4972 tax or a Form 8814 tax reaches line 27, and column (d) of line 16 must carry the annual amount of each. A filer who leaves one out fails this Equal and is refused rather than handed a lower penalty.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part II box C — the filer elects the annualized income installment method
Fact.Description:
The box C election itself: "Your income varied during the year and your penalty is reduced or eliminated when figured using the annualized income installment method. You must figure the penalty using Schedule AI and file Form 2210."
It is a genuine ELECTION — the filer's choice, not a fact the graph can derive. Schedule AI can only ever reduce the penalty (see the induction on the section header), so a filer never harms themselves by electing; but the schedule demands twenty-eight per-period figures the return does not otherwise need, so nobody is made to complete it.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 — box C is checked, complete-safe
Fact.Description:
The box C election with the IsComplete/Switch firewall around it. COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE, and this polarity is the load-bearing decision of the whole unit rather than an inherited shape: an UNANSWERED box C means the filer has NOT elected Schedule AI, so the four column installments take the regular method's flat quarter.
WHY IT MATTERS THAT THIS FACT CAN NEVER BE INCOMPLETE. It is the When of the Switch that every /form2210RequiredInstallmentCol* fact opens with. Were it Incomplete on an unanswered return — the shape a bare Writable read would give — all four column installments would go Incomplete on EVERY return in the corpus, with every value unmoved: a completeness regression that moves no money and breaks the entire penalty chain. The K19 lesson in its purest form, so the polarity is chosen and stated rather than copied.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 — a section 1062(a) farmland-sale election is reported and the penalty would not reflect it
Fact.Description:
Screen text: "You reported a section 1062(a) election to pay the tax on a sale of qualified farmland property in installments (Schedule 3 line 13z, 1062NL). We can't yet figure the estimated tax penalty for a return with this election, so you can't file this return here."
TRUE when Schedule 3 line 13z is labelled 1062NL with a positive amount AND this return computes a positive estimated-tax penalty on Form 2210 or Form 2210-F. The label is the one the Form 1040 instructions prescribe for the 75 percent of the applicable net tax liability from Form 1062 line 14.
WHY IT REFUSES. The election changes the underpayment computation in two printed places this dictionary does not carry. Form 2210 Part I line 3 must include 75 percent of the applicable net tax liability, and estimatedPayments /form2210PartILine3OtherPaymentsAndRefundableCredits does not read line 13z; without it line 4, line 9 and every required installment are too large. A box C filer must also reduce each Schedule AI period's line 14 tax by the same amount, but only for periods that include the qualified sale or exchange, and no fact records the sale date. Both omissions over-state the penalty, so a return that computes NO penalty is not affected: the correct penalty can only be lower, and the guard stays FALSE there.
COMPLETE-SAFE: every leg is IsComplete-first, so an unanswered line 13z, an Incomplete penalty or a non-farmer return with no Form 2210-F figure leaves this FALSE. Residue: a filer who labels the amount otherwise than 1062NL is not detected; the application should offer 1062NL as a fixed choice for the line 13z label.
RETIRES when Part I line 3 adds the 1062NL amount and Schedule AI line 14 takes a per-period reduction keyed on the sale date.

Fact.Name: Does this return cover a tax year other than January 1 through December 31, 2025?
Fact.Description:
Question: "Does this return cover a tax year other than January 1 through December 31, 2025 (a fiscal year, or a short tax year of less than 12 months)?" Help text: most individuals file for the calendar year; answer yes only if your tax year begins on a date other than January 1 or runs for less than 12 months.
Read only by /knockoutForm2210NonCalendarTaxYearNotBuilt. Unanswered means calendar year: the knockout is complete-safe FALSE until the filer answers yes.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 — a fiscal-year or short-year return cannot be figured here
Fact.Description:
Screen text: "You told us this return covers a tax year other than January 1 through December 31, 2025. We can only figure estimated tax payments and the underpayment penalty for a calendar-year return, so you can't file this return here."
TRUE when /writableForm2210TaxYearOtherThanCalendarYear2025 is answered yes. Every installment due date in this module and in estimatedPayments is a calendar-year date literal (the printed Form 2210 due dates 4/15/25, 6/15/25, 9/15/25 and 1/15/26), and no fact records a taxable-year start. Section 6654(k)(1) substitutes the corresponding months for a fiscal year, so a fiscal-year filer's four due dates, the day counts of the penalty worksheet and the Schedule AI period boundaries are all wrong in either direction. Section 6654(k)(2) defers a short taxable year wholly to regulations, and no section 6654 or section 443 regulation is vendored, so a short year cannot be built from a cited rule at all.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE when unanswered. RETIRES when a taxable-year start is modelled and every installment date reads it (fiscal year), and when the governing short-year regulation is vendored and built (short year).

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F — a farmer's single-installment penalty cannot be figured from the answers given
Fact.Description:
Screen text: "You qualify as a farmer or fisher for the estimated tax penalty, so the penalty is figured on Form 2210-F with one installment due January 15, 2026. Finish the Form 2210-F questions (the date you paid and the days from January 15) before you file."
TRUE when /form2210FarmerSingleInstallmentRouteRequired holds, /form2210FLine16Penalty is Incomplete, and /form2210Penalty (the ordinary four-installment figure) is Complete. That is exactly the state in which taxCalculations /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg skips its farmer arm, whose guard needs a Complete Form 2210-F line 16, and falls through to the four-installment penalty that section 6654(i)(1) replaces for this filer. The fall-through figure is a real number on the wrong form, so it would file silently.
A MISSING-INPUT GUARD, NOT A SCOPE KNOCKOUT: the farmer route is fully built and computes as soon as the Form 2210-F inputs are answered, so this blocks submission without joining flow /flowIsKnockedOut, in the shape /form2210ScheduleAiElectedButUnsubstantiated ships. When /form2210Penalty is itself Incomplete (the prior-year-unattested class) the leg reaches its $0 case exactly as it does for a non-farmer, and this stays FALSE.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Schedule AI — the second spouse's Part II cannot be printed
Fact.Description:
Screen text: "You chose the annualized income installment method (Form 2210 box C) and your spouse has self-employment tax in Schedule AI Part II. The IRS requires a separate Schedule AI Part II for each spouse, and we can't yet print the second one, so you can't file this return here."
TRUE when box C is elected (/form2210ElectsScheduleAi), the return is married filing jointly, and the second spouse's Part II line 36 is positive in any column. Line 15 of Part I then carries the COMBINED line 36 figure the instructions require, while the printed Schedule AI has one Part II grid, which carries the primary filer's figures only. The computation is right; the filed form would not foot, and the instructions require a separate Part II for each spouse. When the second spouse's line 36 is zero in every column, the single printed grid foots and this stays FALSE.
COMPLETE-SAFE: each column leg is IsComplete-first. RETIRES with /form2210ScheduleAiLine28PrintedSecondary and its second generated Part II page (the successor contract in the records file).

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Schedule AI — box C with Schedule J income averaging cannot be figured here
Fact.Description:
Screen text: "You chose the annualized income installment method (Form 2210 box C) and you figure your tax with farm income averaging (Schedule J). We can't yet figure the annualized tax for each period with Schedule J, so you can't file this return here. You can uncheck box C and use the regular method."
TRUE when box C is elected (/form2210ElectsScheduleAi) and scheduleJ /scheduleJApplies is true. Schedule J is one of the routes the Schedule AI line 14 instructions name, and no per-period Schedule J computation exists, so line 14 is declined for this return (the Schedule J legs of /form2210ScheduleAiExactLadderFenceSatisfied and the four /form2210ScheduleAiPreferentialCharacterInputsCompleteCol* facts). Both facts it reads are complete-safe, so this is Complete FALSE on every return that does not elect box C or Schedule J.
RETIRES with a per-period Schedule J computation at line 14, together with those five legs.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 — box C is checked but the return cannot substantiate the election
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the filer checked box C and this return’s Schedule AI does not hold up: the line 14 route substantiation, the Part I attestation reconciliation or the Part II attestation reconciliation is false or unanswered, or the Part II separate-Schedule-SE net earnings are not substantiated. A user-input CONTRADICTION guard, in the shape /claimedSpouseCombatPayWithoutMFJ ships: the return asserts an election it does not carry the data for.
WHAT IT CLOSES — A FALSE ALLOWANCE, MEASURED. /form2210RequiredInstallmentCol* switches on Not(/form2210ElectsScheduleAi); the ELECTED arm reads /form2210ScheduleAiLine27Col*, whose Switch has one case and no fallthrough, so any fence miss makes it Incomplete; /form2210Penalty then cannot compute; and taxCalculations /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg gates on IsComplete and falls to a hard Dollar 0.
WHY THE REFUSAL-BY-INCOMPLETENESS PRECEDENT DOES NOT COVER IT. That precedent — used at line 27 itself, and by /form2210Penalty for the payment detail it cannot carry — is honest for a population whose penalty this dictionary CANNOT compute: the form’s own default is that the IRS will figure it and send a bill. This population is the opposite one. Its penalty IS computable, by the regular method, from data the return already holds. An Incomplete there does not read as "not computed"; it reads as $0 at the balance, which is a claim the return does not support.
THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE FOUR SUBSTANTIATION LEGS, NOT THE COMPLETENESS OF LINE 27, and that is the load-bearing choice here. Gating on Not(IsComplete(/form2210ScheduleAiLine27ColD)) would have been simpler and WRONG: line 27 also goes Incomplete when /form2210RequiredInstallment is, i.e. whenever the prior-year attestation is unanswered — a population that legitimately reaches the $0 leg today under the refusal precedent above, and that this guard must not block. Reading the four legs directly separates a Schedule AI that does not substantiate its election from a Part I line 9 that is not evaluable on any method.
THE FIRST LEG read /form2210ScheduleAiExactLadderFenceSatisfied until the period-specific preferential worksheets landed, and this paragraph called it THE FENCE throughout. It is now /form2210ScheduleAiLine14SubstantiatedForEveryColumn. The old leg blocked a box C filer with qualified dividends or a net capital gain from submitting at all, however completely the return answered Schedule AI, because the fence reads the ANNUAL preferential figures and can never be true for that filer; the Schedule AI line 14 instructions name the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet and the Schedule D Tax Worksheet among the routes to use, and this module computes both per period, so the block had no authority left behind it. Witness of the corrected state: node-test form2210/schedule-ai-elected-period-qdcg-worksheets-substantiate-the-election, which holds the old fence Complete false beside this guard Complete false on one elected return.
COMPLETE-SAFE, ALWAYS, and it has to be: each fence leg can itself be Incomplete (Part I’s is, on every return that answers no attestations), and an Incomplete guard would not fire at all — which is exactly the state this exists to catch. The IsComplete conjuncts turn every leg into a Complete Boolean before the All sees it, so an elected return with NOTHING filled in is blocked rather than silently zeroed. /form2210ElectsScheduleAi is complete-safe FALSE, so on every return that does not check box C this resolves Complete false and nothing changes — measured, not assumed: the capture a25-schedule-ai-election-guard holds this fact Complete false on all 942 committed cases, because no committed scenario checks box C.
Checking a box moved $131 of penalty to zero. It still does — the arithmetic is untouched — but the return can no longer be submitted in that state.
A SUBMISSION BLOCK, NOT A SCOPE KNOCKOUT. It carries BlockSubmissionOnTrue and is NOT a member of flow /flowIsKnockedOut: nothing here is unmodelled, so there is no scope limit to explain and nothing to revisit when coverage grows. Its scope-sidecar row records the permanent-non-scope-guard shape (revisit_trigger beginning "n/a"), which is the lint_dual_wiring category that excuses the single wiring.
WHAT WAS REJECTED. (1) Falling the elected arm back to the regular method when the fence fails: box C’s own printed text is "You must figure the penalty using Schedule Al and file Form 2210", so a return that elects it and cannot complete it is not a return the form lets us quietly re-route. (2) Making /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg propagate Incomplete instead of zero: that leg’s zero arm serves every legitimately refused return — the prior-year-unattested class, the returns whose dated payments do not reconcile, the over-capacity line 1b lists — and propagating would take /balanceDue and /finalTaxAmount Incomplete on all of them, a completeness regression across hundreds of committed returns to fix a state none of them are in.
The fourth leg is named wrongly in the first paragraph and the Derived below is what governs. The leg is /form2210ScheduleAiPart2SeparateScheduleSeNetEarningsSubstantiated, read under the same IsComplete/value pair as the other three. It is TRUE in TWO states, not one: when the church-employee separate-Schedule-SE route is not required at all, and when it IS required and the filer has substantiated it. "the church-employee separate-Schedule-SE route is required" therefore does not describe when this guard fires; a required-and-substantiated route passes the fence and blocks nothing. Nothing in the Derived reads /form2210ScheduleAiPart2SeparateScheduleSeRouteRequired's value. Witnesses: node-test form2210/schedule-ai-part2-required-and-substantiated-route-passes-the-fence holds RouteRequired Complete true beside this fact Complete false, and form2210/schedule-ai-part2-church-income-above-the-5b-floor-still-demands-attestations holds it Complete true on the unsubstantiated half.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 23, column (a)
Fact.Description: Line 23 = line 21 minus line 22, floored at zero: the part of this period's annualized demand that the previous columns have not already installed. In column (a) line 22 is structurally zero, so this is line 21 floored.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 26, column (a) — the running allowance
Fact.Description:
Line 26 = lines 24 + 25. Column (a) has no previous column, so line 25 is structurally zero and line 26 is line 24 alone — which IS /form2210RequiredInstallment.
Read as a whole, line 26 in column i equals i times the regular installment less everything already installed — the ceiling that makes Schedule AI incapable of demanding more than the regular method by any due date.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 27, column (a) — the annualized income installment
Fact.Description:
Line 27: "Enter the smaller of line 23 or line 26 here and on Form 2210, Part III, line 10." Column (a)'s annualized income installment — the figure that REPLACES the regular method's flat quarter when box C is checked.
THE FENCE SITS HERE, gathering every leg the schedule needs, and it refuses by INCOMPLETENESS: the Switch has one case and no fallthrough, so when any leg fails or is unanswered this line resolves Incomplete, /form2210RequiredInstallmentColA falls through to it, and /form2210Penalty lands on the form's own default ("the IRS will figure it and send you a bill"). The four legs are /form2210ScheduleAiLine14SubstantiatedForEveryColumn, the Part I attestation consistency, the Part II attestation consistency, and the Part II separate-Schedule-SE net-earnings substantiation.
THE FIRST LEG named above was the exact-ladder fence on line 14 until the period-specific preferential worksheets landed. That fence reads the ANNUAL qualified dividend and capital gain figures, so it stayed FALSE on every box C filer who holds either and answers the period character amounts, even though line 14 computed a tax for them in all four columns. The refusal took this line Incomplete, took /form2210Penalty with it and dropped the Form 1040 line 38 estimated-tax leg to a hard zero, on a population the Schedule AI line 14 instructions tell us to compute. The leg is now /form2210ScheduleAiLine14SubstantiatedForEveryColumn, TRUE exactly when line 14 reached a tax by a supported route in every column. The exact ladder is one of those routes, so nothing the old fence admitted is turned away now, and the quantities it turned away for good reason are still read one level down.
NOT A KNOCKOUT, deliberately. These returns file correctly today: Schedule AI is elective and declining it only ever leaves the penalty at or above the annualized figure. A refusal by incompleteness is the same instrument /form2210Penalty already uses for the payment detail it cannot carry.
The fourth leg is named wrongly above and the Derived below is what governs. The leg is not "the absence of the church-employee separate-Schedule-SE route"; it is /form2210ScheduleAiPart2SeparateScheduleSeNetEarningsSubstantiated, which is TRUE both when that route is absent AND when it is required and substantiated. A filer on the church route who supplies the per-period allocations passes this leg; only an unsubstantiated route fails it. Nothing here reads /form2210ScheduleAiPart2SeparateScheduleSeRouteRequired's value. Witness: node-test form2210/schedule-ai-part2-required-and-substantiated-route-passes-the-fence holds RouteRequired Complete true beside /form2210ScheduleAiPart2SeparateScheduleSeNetEarningsSubstantiated Complete true.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part III line 10, column (a) — required installment
Fact.Description:
Part III line 10 in column (a), stated as the printed line states it: "If box C in Part II applies, enter the amounts from Schedule AI, line 27. Otherwise, enter 25% (0.25) of line 9, Form 2210, in each column."
THE UNELECTED ARM READS /form2210RequiredInstallment ITSELF, not a re-derivation of 25% of the required annual payment, and that is the whole design of this re-point rather than a convenience. Identical dependency means identical VALUE and identical COMPLETENESS — including the Incomplete that the prior-year-unattested population already resolves — so every return that does not check box C is untouched BY CONSTRUCTION and not merely by measurement. /form2210RequiredInstallment is kept rather than replaced for the same reason: deleting it would move 942 committed rows and force edits to seventeen assert files that currently pin it, and those files staying green untouched IS the re-point's cheapest proof.
THE ELECTED ARM CAN BE INCOMPLETE, and that is the refusal, not a defect: a filer who checks box C but whose return fails the Schedule AI fence gets no penalty figure rather than a wrong one.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 12 — the printed zero, the same figure in every column
Fact.Description:
Line 12: "Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR filers, enter -0- in each column." Every return this dictionary files is a Form 1040 or Form 1040-SR return, so the printed figure is zero in all four columns, and ONE fact serves all four exactly as /form2210ScheduleAiLine7 does for the standard deduction.
WHY IT EXISTS NOW. /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColA and its siblings deliberately state line 13 as the floor of line 11 alone, reasoning that a fact whose only possible value is zero and whose only reader would be line 13 is a cost with no benefit. That reasoning was about the ARITHMETIC and it still holds: nothing reads this fact and line 13 must not be re-pointed at it. What it did not cover is the PRINTED BOX. Form 2210 page 3 carries four fillable line 12 boxes and the register had no fact to put in them, so the schedule printed blank where the form says -0-. This fact is print only by design, not a partial build waiting on a rewire.
It resolves on every return the form prints on, elected or not, which is the standing /form2210ScheduleAiLine7 already has: that fact aliases /standardDeduction and is therefore complete whenever the return is.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 22, column (a) — no previous column to total
Fact.Description:
Line 22: "Enter the total of the amounts in all previous columns of line 27." Column (a) is the first column, so there are no previous columns and the total is zero.
/form2210ScheduleAiLine23ColA already states this in prose ("In column (a) line 22 is structurally zero, so this is line 21 floored") and computes correctly without reading anything: this fact carries that zero for the PRINTED BOX only, which the register otherwise leaves blank. Line 23 column (a) stays exactly as it is; nothing is owed and nothing is rewired.
Columns (b), (c) and (d) are real Add facts (/form2210ScheduleAiLine22ColB and its siblings) because there the printed total has terms; only column (a) is empty by position.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part I line 25, column (a) — no previous column to carry forward
Fact.Description:
Line 25: "Subtract line 27 of the previous column from line 26 of that column." Column (a) has no previous column, so nothing carries forward and the printed figure is zero.
/form2210ScheduleAiLine26ColA already states this in prose ("Column (a) has no previous column, so line 25 is structurally zero and line 26 is line 24 alone") and reads /form2210RequiredInstallment directly: this fact carries the zero for the PRINTED BOX only. Line 26 column (a) stays exactly as it is; nothing is owed and nothing is rewired.
Columns (b), (c) and (d) are real Subtract facts (/form2210ScheduleAiLine25ColB and its siblings), the unused allowance the method carries forward; only column (a) is empty by position.

Fact.Name: Schedule AI Part II line 28 as printed, primary filer, column (a) — net earnings from self-employment for 1/1/25-3/31/25
Fact.Description:
The value the printed line-28 box carries for column (a): the primary filer's net earnings from self-employment for the cumulative period, on either of the two routes the instructions allow.
WHY THIS IS NOT /form2210ScheduleAiLine28AppliedPrimaryColA. That fact is the ordinary route only — the attested per-period figure with the $400 floor. On the church-employee route the instructions send the filer to "a separate Schedule SE as a worksheet to calculate net earnings from self-employment for each period", and its line 6 is what goes on line 28. The module already computes that combined figure as /form2210ScheduleAiSeparateScheduleSeLine6PrimaryColA = Add(line-28 applied, separate-Schedule-SE line 5b), and it is that figure — not the ordinary-route one — that lines 33 and 35 consume. So the printed box must show it too, or the printed column would not foot for a church-employee filer.
It reduces to the ordinary-route figure exactly when there is no church employee income, because the line-5b component falls through to a hard zero, so nothing changes for the ordinary filer.
This is a form2210 alias of a form2210SeparateScheduleSE fact because IRS2210 declares form2210 and estimatedPayments only; the driver adds the module= attribute.
