Fact.Description: Box A of Part II, "You request a waiver (see instructions) of your entire penalty. You must check this box and file page 1 of Form 2210, but you aren't required to figure your penalty." It is a request the filer makes, on grounds the Secretary decides (retirement after 62 or disability with reasonable cause, or a casualty, disaster or other unusual circumstance), and nothing on the return can derive it, so it is the filer's own entry. Checking it changes what the filer must attach rather than any figure this dictionary computes: the penalty is not figured at all, and the supporting statement the instructions require is outside the fact graph. This box is READ, and by the route that decides which underpayment form figures the penalty: /form2210FPartIBoxARequestsWaiver reads it, /form2210FRequiredForReturn reads that, and taxCalculations /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg reads that in turn to choose between the Form 2210-F chain and form2210 /form2210Penalty. /form2210Penalty itself does not read this box; the leg that carries a penalty to Form 1040 line 38 does.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part II box B: the filer requests a waiver of part of the penalty
Fact.Description: Box B of Part II, "You request a waiver (see instructions) of part of your penalty. You must figure your penalty and waiver amount and file Form 2210." A distinct election from box A: box A files page 1 alone and figures nothing, while box B requires the whole form to be figured without regard to the waiver and the waived amount to be written in parentheses beside line 19. It is the filer's own request on grounds the Secretary decides, so it is an intake. The waived AMOUNT is a separate figure the instructions have the filer subtract on line 19, and this dictionary asks for it: /form2210WritablePartIILine19WaiverAmountRequested carries it and /form2210Line19WaiverAmountApplied subtracts it inside /form2210Penalty, so checking this box DOES change the computed value. Checking it and leaving the amount blank waives nothing, so the gross penalty stands; the screen treats the amount as required once this box is checked.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 line 19 dotted line: the part of the penalty the filer asks the IRS to waive
Fact.Description:
SCREEN. Ask "How much of the penalty are you asking the IRS to waive?" — a dollar amount, shown only to a filer who has checked Part II box B.
HELP TEXT. "You checked box B, so you are asking the IRS to waive PART of your penalty. The instructions have you figure the penalty as if there were no waiver, write the amount you want waived in parentheses on the dotted line next to line 19, subtract it, and enter the result on line 19. Enter the amount you are asking to have waived. You must also attach a statement to your return explaining why you could not meet the estimated tax requirements and the period the request covers; if you are asking because of retirement after age 62 or disability, attach documentation of the date; if because of a casualty, disaster or other unusual circumstance, attach documentation such as police or insurance reports. The IRS decides whether to grant the request." (2025 Instructions for Form 2210, "How To Figure Your Penalty ... Waiver of Penalty", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i2210.pdf, page 2.)
ASKED WHEN /form2210WritablePartIIBoxBRequestsPartialPenaltyWaiver is answered TRUE. It is not asked of a box-A filer: box A waives the ENTIRE penalty and the printed instruction says that filer is not required to figure it at all.
UNANSWERED POSTURE — NOTHING IS WAIVED and the gross penalty stands on the return. This is the conservative direction and it is chosen rather than inherited: refusing instead would leave /form2210Penalty unresolved, and taxCalculations /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg answers a hard $0 in that case, so a blank here would silently waive the whole penalty of a filer who asked for only part of it. The screen must therefore treat this as REQUIRED once box B is checked — the printed form demands the number and this dictionary cannot derive it — but the return stays filable and over-states rather than under-states the penalty if the screen is skipped.
VALIDATION. Dollar, Min $0. There is no Max on the intake because a Limit takes a literal and the bound here is a computed figure; the bound is applied downstream instead, where /form2210Line19WaiverAmountApplied takes the LESSER of this amount and the penalty figured without regard to the waiver, so a request larger than the penalty waives all of it and never produces a negative line 19. Zero is accepted and means the filer checked box B but is asking for nothing, which subtracts nothing. The screen SHOULD show the computed gross penalty beside the question so the filer can see what they are asking against.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS. /form2210Line19WaiverAmountApplied, which /form2210Penalty subtracts from /form2210PenaltyWorksheetTotal, so it reaches printed line 19, taxCalculations /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg, Form 1040 line 38, /balanceDue and /finalTaxAmount. The supporting statement itself is outside the fact graph.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 line 19 — the waived amount actually subtracted from the computed penalty
Fact.Description:
The amount Form 2210 line 19 subtracts from the penalty figured without regard to a waiver. It is the filer's requested amount when Part II box B is checked and the request is a figure this return can honour, and $0 whenever box B is not checked.
BOX B IS THE ONE PART II BOX THAT DEMANDS ARITHMETIC, which is why this fact exists and box A needs no counterpart. Box A's printed instruction says the filer "aren't required to figure your penalty"; box B's says to figure the whole penalty without regard to the waiver, write the waived amount in parentheses beside line 19, subtract it, and enter the result. The election was already captured; the amount it elects was not, so line 19 and Form 1040 line 38 carried the GROSS figure and the filer was charged exactly the amount they had asked to have waived.
NEITHER GAP REFUSES, and that is a decision taken against the obvious instinct because the measurement went the other way. Box B checked with the amount still unanswered leaves the GROSS penalty standing rather than refusing: a refusal here does not reach the filer as a refusal, because taxCalculations /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg's terminal case answers a hard $0 whenever /form2210Penalty does not resolve, so refusing would silently waive the ENTIRE penalty of a filer who asked to have only part of it waived — a bigger error, in the opposite direction, than the one this fact exists to fix. The unanswered amount is the intake screen's problem, and the screen demands it.
A REQUEST LARGER THAN THE COMPUTED PENALTY IS TAKEN DOWN TO THE PENALTY, not refused, for the same reason and one more: no filer can be waived more than they owe, so LesserOf is the reading the printed subtraction already implies, and it cannot produce a negative line 19.
EVERY CASE RETURNS A DOLLAR SHAPE, not a completeness guarantee. On the arm where box B is checked and an amount is entered, this fact is LesserOf the request and /form2210PenaltyWorksheetTotal, so it inherits that total's completeness — the same completeness /form2210Penalty's own computed arm already has, so this fact makes no return Incomplete that was not already. A return that does not elect the waiver resolves $0 and is byte-identical to one built before this fact existed.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part II box D: withholding treated as paid on the dates actually withheld
Fact.Description: Box D of Part II, "Your penalty is lower when figured by treating the federal income tax withheld from your income as paid on the dates it was actually withheld, instead of in equal amounts on the payment due dates." The statute makes withholding deemed paid in equal parts on each due date UNLESS the taxpayer establishes the dates on which the amounts were actually withheld, so the box is the taxpayer's election to establish them, which no return figure can derive. THIS RETURN RECORDS THE ELECTION AND FIGURES THE PENALTY ON THE STATUTORY QUARTER DEFAULT, and that is law-correct rather than an omission. Section 6654(g)(1) makes one-fourth-per-due-date the DEFAULT and actual dates an election available only "unless the taxpayer establishes the dates on which all amounts were actually withheld". When the box is checked, the three column entries /form2210WritableBoxDWithholdingColumnA through C establish the dates: /form2210BoxDWithholdingActualDatesEstablished then routes the withholding half of line 11 to the actual windows, column (d) taking the remainder. Checked with those entries unanswered, inconsistent or negative, line 11 keeps the statutory one-fourth default, which is what the statute directs when the dates are not established.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part II box E: joint for 2024 or 2025 but not both, with line 8 under line 5
Fact.Description: Box E of Part II, "You filed or are filing a joint return for either 2024 or 2025, but not for both years, and line 8 above is smaller than line 5 above." The first half turns on the 2024 filing status, which a single-year dictionary does not hold: estimatedPayments carries only the two attested prior-year figures /form2210PriorYearTax and /form2210PriorYearAgi, and nothing else about 2024. The whole box is therefore the filer's own entry rather than half derived, and the second half is left to the filer to read off the two printed lines above it. Checking it lets a filer file page 1 alone without figuring the penalty, so it changes what is filed rather than any figure this dictionary computes.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F Part I box A: the filer requests a waiver
Fact.Description: Form 2210-F box A, checked by a filer who requests a waiver of the penalty. Form 2210 splits the same request into its box A (the entire penalty) and box B (part of it), and either request is a waiver request on this form, so this reads both of those intakes.

Fact.Name: This return's estimated-tax penalty is figured on the farmer's single January-15 installment
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the filer is a farmer or fisher under section 6654(i)(2) and has NOT met the second printed test. Section 6654(i)(1) then replaces the ordinary four quarterly installments with ONE: "there shall be only 1 required installment for the taxable year", due 15 January 2026, in the amount of the required annual payment figured with 66 2/3 percent for 90 percent and without regard to subparagraph (C) of subsection (d)(1). That is a different computation, not a different presentation of the same one, and it is what Form 2210-F prints.
WHY TEST 2 IS A NEGATIVE CONJUNCT RATHER THAN A SEPARATE GATE. A farmer who ALSO filed and paid the entire tax due by 2 March 2026 owes no penalty at all - the waiver, already an exit of estimatedPayments:/isExemptFromEstimatedTaxPenalty - so there is nothing for this route to figure. Test 2 is complete-safe FALSE, so an unanswered test 2 leaves the route REQUIRED and the penalty charged, which is the adverse-safe direction: silence does not grant a waiver.
THE 110 PERCENT RESIDUE, NAMED HERE BECAUSE THIS IS THE FACT THAT WOULD REMOVE IT. Section 6654(i)(1)(C) disapplies subsection (d)(1)(C) - the 110 percent uplift for a prior-year AGI over the threshold - for a farmer, and Form 2210-F line 10 prints the bare 2024 tax with no uplift, which /form2210FLine11RequiredAnnualPayment already follows. The REGULAR form's line 8 has no farmer clause in its printed instruction, and estimatedPayments:/form2210PriorYearRequiredPayment therefore still applies 110 percent to a farmer on the strength of /form2210PriorYearAgiExceedsThreshold alone. The disapplication is the ROUTE's, not a regular-form arm: a farmer whose penalty is figured on this route never reaches that line. Until a consumer reads this fact, a farmer figured on the regular form keeps the 110 percent uplift, and that residue is real.

Fact.Name: This return files Form 2210-F
Fact.Description:
True when the filer is a FARMER OR FISHER under section 6654(i)(2) and either Part I box applies. Both halves are printed conditions: the form's own title and its Part I instruction are addressed to farmers and fishermen, and the box is what makes such a filer file the form at all. It is the render gate the form needs in dictionary/pdf/2025/gates.tsv.
THE FARMER CONJUNCT IS WHAT STOPS A NON-FARMER RENDERING FORM 2210-F. Without it this fact was Any(box A, box E) alone, with no farmer test anywhere in it, so an ordinary filer who requested a penalty waiver flipped it true, rendered Form 2210-F, and had the return's penalty figured on the farmer's single January-15 installment instead of the four quarterly ones. The two forms answer different questions and their line 9 exits are different definitions, so that was a real substitution and not a presentation choice.
IT STOPS 2210-F RENDERING AND DOES NOT BY ITSELF START FORM 2210 RENDERING. A non-farmer who checks box A renders neither form from this fact; Form 2210's own render conditions are elsewhere.

Fact.Name: The 365 day denominator of the Form 2210-F penalty
Fact.Description: The denominator the printed line 16 divides the day count by.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 11: required annual payment
Fact.Description:
Form 2210-F line 11, the smaller of line 7 and line 10. A farmer or fisher's prior year leg is the tax shown on the 2024 return with no 110 percent substitution, so this reads the attested estimatedPayments:/form2210PriorYearTax directly rather than estimatedPayments:/form2210PriorYearRequiredPayment.
THE DISAPPLICATION REACHES THIS LINE TOO, and the route is the statute rather than the printed page. Section 6654(i)(1)(C) figures the farmer's single installment "under subsection (d)(1)(B)", and that subparagraph's flush text disapplies the prior-year leg for a filer who did not file a 2024 return or whose 2024 year was shorter than 12 months. So when estimatedPayments:/form2210PriorYearSafeHarborDisapplied is true this line is line 7 alone, exactly as the regular form's line 9 becomes line 5 alone. Without it a farmer with a short 2024 year or no 2024 return who attests a small or zero 2024 tax would keep a safe harbor the statute takes away, and every figure below would be too small in the taxpayer's favour.
THE ANSWERED-ZERO ARM THE REGULAR FORM'S LINE 8 CARRIES IS NOT NEEDED HERE. That arm exists because the regular form multiplies the 2024 tax by 100 or 110 percent and the percentage needs the 2024 AGI; this line applies no percentage at all — (i)(1)(C) figures the amount "without regard to subparagraph (C) of subsection (d)(1)" — so an attested $0 resolves here already, with no AGI read.
THE PRINTED LINE-11 INSTRUCTION IS NOT VENDORED. sources/ carries the 2025 Form 2210-F but not its instructions, so the disapplication is taken from the statute the form implements and the printed wording is not quoted.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F estimated payments made by January 15
Fact.Description: Estimated tax and prior-year overpayment credits paid on or before January 15, 2026, from the dated decomposition of Form 1040 line 26. All four regular-form payment windows together end on that date. The dated detail must reconcile to the annual total. Missing detail or an unanswered date leaves this amount Incomplete. A settled no-payment answer that reconciles to zero makes payment dates moot.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 12: estimated payments and withholding
Fact.Description: Form 2210-F line 12, the estimated tax payments made by January 15, 2026 plus the federal income tax and excess social security or tier 1 railroad retirement tax withheld during 2025. /estimatedAndFromLastYear is the annual estimated tax figure and is not filtered by the January 15 date, so a payment made after that date is included here and the underpayment on line 13 is understated for that filer. The date-filtered computation now uses /form2210FEstimatedPaymentsByJanuary15 instead of that annual scalar; a late payment cannot reduce this line, and unresolved payment timing leaves it Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 13: the underpayment
Fact.Description:
Form 2210-F line 13, line 11 less line 12, FLOORED AT ZERO because the printed line says so: "Underpayment. Subtract line 12 from line 11. If the result is zero or less, stop here; you don't owe the penalty." A farmer who paid MORE than the required annual payment has no underpayment, not a negative one.
THE FLOOR IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN COSMETIC, and it is the same floor every analogue on the Form 2210 side already carries (/form2210UnderpaymentColA-ColD, /form2210OverpaymentColA- ColC, /form2210Line15ColB-ColD, /form2210Line16ColB-ColD, /form2210PenaltyWorksheetTotal). Section 6654(a) makes the figure an ADDITION to tax, so it has no negative branch. Without the floor an overpaying farmer carried a negative underpayment into line 16, and because taxCalculations /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg gates on IsComplete rather than on sign, and /balanceDue is Round(GreaterOf(totalTax + that leg - totalPayments, 0)), the negative penalty arrived as a REDUCTION of the tax owed — an amount the return had no basis to claim.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 16: the penalty
Fact.Description: Form 2210-F line 16, the underpayment on line 13 times the days on line 15 over 365 times 0.07, which the filer enters on Form 1040 line 38. The 0.07 is the rate the TY2025 form prints and is not derived from section 6621; a later year must re read it. Because each step rounds to whole dollars the result can differ from the printed one by under a dollar. IT REACHES THE RETURN (reconciliation unit W3): taxCalculations /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg gained a farmer and fisher arm that reads this fact when /form2210FRequiredForReturn is true and this penalty resolves, so the amount now reaches /balanceDue, /finalTaxAmount and Form 1040 line 38. The sentence this replaces said the fact was print only and that /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg carried the Form 2210 amount for every filer, farmer or not, which was true until that unit. THE PRINTED LINE 9 NO PENALTY EXIT IS ALSO APPLIED HERE, as the first arm below.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 16 first step: the underpayment prorated over the days
Fact.Description: The underpayment on line 13 multiplied by the day count on line 15 over 365, the first of the two factors the printed line 16 applies. It is a separate fact because the engine rounds to whole dollars at each step, so naming the intermediate makes the rounding visible.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 3: tax after credits plus other taxes
Fact.Description: Form 2210-F line 3, the sum of line 1 (tax after credits, Form 1040 line 22) and line 2 (other taxes). It reads the two Form 2210 Part I legs staged for the same printed captions rather than aliasing /totalTax, because those legs are the exact figures the two printed lines above it show.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 6: current year tax
Fact.Description: Form 2210-F line 6, line 3 less the refundable credits on line 4. Line 5 is reserved and adds nothing. This is the figure the two thirds leg of the farmer's required annual payment is taken from.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 7: two thirds of the current year tax
Fact.Description: Form 2210-F line 7, line 6 multiplied by 66 and two thirds percent. The factor is the exact fraction 2/3, not the 0.667 the printed line offers for hand computation, which would understate the requirement by a few cents on a large tax. This mirrors estimatedPayments /form2210NinetyPercentOfCurrentYearTax, which already substitutes 2/3 for a farmer or fisher.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 9: current year tax less withholding
Fact.Description: Form 2210-F line 9, line 6 less the withholding on line 8. Less than 1,000 dollars means no penalty is owed. It is not estimatedPayments /form2210BalanceAfterWithholding, which subtracts withholding from the Form 2210 line 4 figure and treats refundable credits as zero.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 14: the date the underpayment was paid
Fact.Description: Form 2210-F line 14, the date the line 13 amount was paid or April 15, 2026, whichever is earlier. The graph's dated payments collection carries estimated tax payments, not the date this particular underpayment was made good, so the date is the filer's own entry. One Day behind the printed month and day boxes; the printed year is fixed at 26 on the form.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 15: number of days from January 15, 2026 to the line 14 date
Fact.Description:
Form 2210-F line 15, the day count the penalty is prorated over, as the filer enters it on the printed line. Ask: "How many days are there from January 15, 2026 to the date you entered on line 14?" Help: line 15 is "Number of days from January 15, 2026, to the date on line 14" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f2210f.pdf, page 1), and line 14 is the date the line 13 underpayment was paid, or April 15, 2026, whichever is earlier — so the answer is between 0 and 90. Asked when Form 2210-F is required for the return and line 13 is above zero; never otherwise. Validation: Dollar, Min 0, Max 90 — 90 is the whole span from January 15 to April 15, 2026, and the printed line 14 cannot name a later date. Unanswered: the count is taken from line 14 instead and the return still files; the screen should PREFILL it from the line 14 date rather than leaving it blank. It feeds /form2210FLine15DaysApplied, which is what line 16 actually prorates by.
IT IS CARRIED AS A DOLLAR rather than an Int because line 16 multiplies the underpayment by it, and the printed field is one box on the form.

Fact.Name: Form 2210-F line 15 as applied: the days from January 15, 2026 to the line 14 date
Fact.Description:
The day count line 16 actually prorates the underpayment by. It is a pure function of the line 14 date, so the graph computes it rather than trusting the entry — the same boundary that keeps Schedule AI line 14 out of the attestation list. When line 14 is unanswered there is nothing to compute from and the filer's own line 15 entry stands, which is the behaviour every return had before this fact existed.
THE LADDER IS THE CALENDAR, NOT AN APPROXIMATION, and it is the shape /form2210DatedEstimatedPayments/*/form2210PaymentDayNumber already ships: consecutive integers from the January 15, 2026 origin, expressed as a month offset plus the day of the month, with every offset checked at the first and last day of its month. January 16 is 1 and January 31 is 16; February 1 is 17 and February 28 is 44 (2026 is not a leap year); March 1 is 45 and March 31 is 75; April 1 is 76 and April 15 is 90. A date on or before January 15, 2026 is 0 — the underpayment was made good before the count starts. A date after April 15, 2026 is 90, because the printed line 14 is "the date the amount on line 13 was paid or April 15, 2026, whichever is earlier" and the count cannot run past its own endpoint.
THE FALLBACK IS CLAMPED TOO. The line 15 writable carries Limit type="Max" 90, but a Limit is intake validation and is not enforced when the graph resolves, so the fallback takes the LESSER of 90 and the entry. The other half of an unreconciled entry is not recoverable here: with no line 14 date there is nothing to compare an understated count against, so a filer who enters 0 gets no penalty prorated over no days. That residue is the reason the screen should prefill line 15 from line 14 rather than leaving it blank.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 is required for this return
Fact.Description:
THE RENDER GATE for Form 2210, and it is the Part II boxes — NOT the penalty. The printed Part II heading says it outright: "Reasons for Filing. Check applicable boxes. If none apply, don't file Form 2210", and the flowchart above it reaches the same place from the other side: "You may owe a penalty. Does any box in Part II below apply? ... No: Don't file Form 2210. You aren't required to figure your penalty because the IRS will figure it and send you a bill for any unpaid amount. If you want to figure it, you may use Part III as a worksheet and enter your penalty amount on your tax return, but don't file Form 2210." A positive penalty is therefore NOT a reason to print this form; a checked box is the only reason.
THE FIVE BOXES, each read complete-safely (the All(IsComplete(x), x) idiom this dictionary uses in 242 places, so an unanswered box reads Complete false rather than Incomplete):
A /form2210WritablePartIIBoxARequestsEntirePenaltyWaiver — "You request a waiver ... of your entire penalty." B /form2210WritablePartIIBoxBRequestsPartialPenaltyWaiver — "You request a waiver ... of part of your penalty." C /form2210ElectsScheduleAi — the module's own complete-safe read of the box C annualized income installment election ("Your income varied during the year and your penalty is reduced or eliminated when figured using the annualized income installment method"). D /form2210WritablePartIIBoxDWithholdingOnActualDates — "Your penalty is lower when figured by treating the federal income tax withheld ... as paid on the dates actually withheld." E /form2210WritablePartIIBoxEJointReturnOnlyOneOfTheTwoYears — "You filed or are filing a joint return for either 2024 or 2025, but not for both years, and line 8 above is smaller than line 5 above."
SCOPE NOTE: box E's printed condition has a second limb (line 8 smaller than line 5) that this gate does not re-derive; the writable is the filer's own checkbox, exactly as boxes A, B and D are. Form 2210-F has its own gate (/form2210FRequiredForReturn, IRS2210F).
Complete-safe by construction: every leg resolves Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: The return shows combat zone or contingency operation service
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the return shows service in, or in support of, the Armed Forces in a combat zone or contingency operation: the Form 1040 combat zone notation is answered yes, OR Form W-2 box 12 code Q nontaxable combat pay totals above $0. Section 7508 postpones the payment of each estimated tax installment for that service plus the next 180 days, and section 7508(c) extends it to the spouse, so either filer's service marks the whole return.
COMPLETE-SAFE: each leg is IsComplete-first, so an unanswered notation or an unanswered or absent W-2 collection leaves its leg FALSE. Residue: a contingency operation, support or hospitalization-only filer who carries no code Q and leaves the notation unanswered is not detected, which is why the notation question is routed to every return; a filer whose code Q pay is for service that ended early enough that the postponed window misses every 2025 installment is detected anyway.
Read by /form2210CombatZoneIrsFiguresPenalty and by form1040 /knockoutForm2210CombatZoneMustFilePostponementNotModeled.

Fact.Name: Form 2210 Part II box B, C or D is checked: the filer must figure the penalty and file the whole form
Fact.Description:
TRUE when Part II box B (a waiver of part of the penalty), box C (the annualized income installment method, read through /form2210ElectsScheduleAi) or box D (withholding treated as paid on the dates actually withheld) is checked. These are the boxes that make the filer figure the penalty and file the whole form; box A (a waiver of the entire penalty) and box E (a joint return for one of 2024 and 2025 only) file page 1 alone and leave the penalty to the IRS unless one of these is also checked.
COMPLETE-SAFE: each box is read with the All(IsComplete(x), x) idiom, and /form2210ElectsScheduleAi is complete-safe by construction, so an unanswered box counts as unchecked.
Read by /form2210CombatZoneIrsFiguresPenalty and by form1040 /knockoutForm2210CombatZoneMustFilePostponementNotModeled.

Fact.Name: Combat zone service and no box that makes the filer figure the penalty: the IRS figures the penalty and the penalty line is left blank
Fact.Description:
Screen text: "You (or your spouse) served in, or in support of, the Armed Forces in a combat zone or contingency operation, or were hospitalized for an injury received there. The due dates for your 2025 estimated tax payments are postponed for that service plus 180 days. We are leaving the estimated tax penalty line on your return blank: the IRS will figure any penalty you owe, taking the postponement into account, and send you a bill. If you checked Form 2210 box A (a waiver of the entire penalty) or box E (a joint return for only one of 2024 and 2025), we file page 1 of Form 2210 with that box checked and the IRS also considers it; otherwise we don't file Form 2210."
TRUE when /form2210CombatZoneServiceShown holds AND none of Part II boxes B, C or D is checked (/form2210PartIIBoxBCOrDChecked) AND no box makes the return file Form 2210-F (/form2210FRequiredForReturn, a farmer or fisher with a Part I box; Form 2210-F has no page-1-only filing, so its boxes need the line 16 figure). Form 2210 gives every filer who checks none of boxes B, C or D the choice to let the IRS figure the penalty: with no box, leave the penalty line blank and do not file Form 2210; with box A or E alone, file only page 1 and leave the penalty to the IRS. Form 2210-F says the same for a farmer or fisher who checks neither Part I box. For this population that choice is taken on the filer's behalf, because the penalty this dictionary computes applies the unpostponed installment due dates and counts every day of each underpayment period, so it can only be too high.
WHAT IT DOES. /form2210Penalty and /form2210FLine16Penalty answer $0 from a first case while this is TRUE (the amount the return enters, not a finding that nothing is owed: the IRS bills whatever the postponed computation gives), so taxCalculations /estimatedTaxPenaltyLeg carries $0 to Form 1040 line 38 and the balance due, and the Form 2210-F render gate stays FALSE; the Form 2210 render gate (/form2210RequiredForReturn) is TRUE only for a box A or box E filer, who files page 1.
COMPLETE-SAFE: every leg resolves Complete. /form2210PartIIBoxBCOrDChecked is complete-safe by construction; /form2210FRequiredForReturn is read IsComplete-first, so an unanswered farmer test or Part I box counts as no box.

Fact.Name: Ordinary rate-schedule tax on Schedule AI line 13, column (a)
Fact.Description: The ordinary rate-schedule tax on this column’s rounded line 13. This is the exact existing ladder factored out for reuse: it supplies the line 24 comparison in the period-specific Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet, the line 46 comparison in the period-specific Schedule D Tax Worksheet, and the prior ordinary-ladder fallback. Tax Table midpoint rounding remains in /form2210ScheduleAiLine13RoundedColA.

Fact.Name: Ordinary rate-schedule tax on Schedule AI line 13, column (b)
Fact.Description: The ordinary rate-schedule tax on this column’s rounded line 13. This is the exact existing ladder factored out for reuse: it supplies the line 24 comparison in the period-specific Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet, the line 46 comparison in the period-specific Schedule D Tax Worksheet, and the prior ordinary-ladder fallback. Tax Table midpoint rounding remains in /form2210ScheduleAiLine13RoundedColB.

Fact.Name: Ordinary rate-schedule tax on Schedule AI line 13, column (c)
Fact.Description: The ordinary rate-schedule tax on this column’s rounded line 13. This is the exact existing ladder factored out for reuse: it supplies the line 24 comparison in the period-specific Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet, the line 46 comparison in the period-specific Schedule D Tax Worksheet, and the prior ordinary-ladder fallback. Tax Table midpoint rounding remains in /form2210ScheduleAiLine13RoundedColC.

Fact.Name: Ordinary rate-schedule tax on Schedule AI line 13, column (d)
Fact.Description: The ordinary rate-schedule tax on this column’s rounded line 13. This is the exact existing ladder factored out for reuse: it supplies the line 24 comparison in the period-specific Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet, the line 46 comparison in the period-specific Schedule D Tax Worksheet, and the prior ordinary-ladder fallback. Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 47 — tax on all taxable income — Schedule AI column (a)
Fact.Description:
THE SCHEDULE D TAX WORKSHEET'S FINAL TAX, and the root of the /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine1ColA through /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine46ColA subtree above. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Tax on all taxable income (including capital gains and qualified dividends). Enter the smaller of line 45 or line 46. Also, include this amount on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 16. (If you are filing Form 2555, don't enter this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16. Instead, enter it on line 4 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040.)" This fact IS line 47; there is no separate /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine4ColA7, exactly as /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColA is both the QDCGT's last line and its output.
THE SINGLE ROUND OF THE WHOLE WORKSHEET SITS HERE, matching /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColA's sibling treatment: the per-line children stay unrounded so the 15%, 20%, 25% and 28% multiplications (lines 31, 34, 40 and 43) do not each accumulate a rounding error before line 45 sums them. TWO EXCEPTIONS, stated so the claim is not read as absolute — lines 44 and 46 are rate-schedule taxes and each arrives already rounded from the fact that computes it (/form2210ScheduleAiSdtwOrdinaryTaxOnLine21ColA and form2210 /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColA). Rounding a whole-dollar table lookup is part of computing it, not an early truncation of an intermediate.
THAT PRE-ROUNDING IS NOT COSMETIC, and the tests say so: on sdtw-tax-boundary-line19-threshold-one-dollar-over, line 45 is $40,199.25 and line 46 is $40,199, so the lesser-of picks line 46 — the extra dollar's 25% tax loses to a line 46 that was rounded down from $40,199.32. A reviewer changing where the Round sits will break that case, which is the point of it.
THE FORM 2555 CARVE-OUT, BOTH HALVES, AND BOTH ARE NOW IMPLEMENTED — BY A SECOND WORKSHEET, NOT BY THIS ONE. Line 47's own text redirects the RESULT away from Form 1040 line 16 for a Form 2555 filer, and worksheet line 1 (:1084-1086) redirects the INPUT the same way ("if you are filing Form 2555 ... enter instead the amount from line 3 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet"); the same footnote hangs off lines 6, 9 and 11 (:1173-1174). The footnote does not ask this worksheet to change — it asks for a SECOND run, "in its entirety and with the following additional modifications" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37), whose modifications are "to be made only for purposes of filling out the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet above". That second run is /feiScheduleDTaxWorksheetTax and the /feiSdtw* lineage below, and its root is taken by preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4 on the arm that fires on /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet. THIS fact is the first run and keeps its unsubstituted input and its Form 1040 line 16 destination, which is right for every filer who is not completing that worksheet — and for the filer who is, taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome pre-empts the arm that reads this fact, so it never figures line 16 for them.
COMPUTED ON EVERY RETURN, DELIBERATELY. /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet is NOT a term of this fact: it decides WHICH worksheet figures Form 1040 line 16, and that decision belongs to the consumer. Gating this fact on it would make the SDTW resolve to a fictitious $0 on every QDCGT return, which is worse than an honest "what the SDTW would produce". On a return with no preferential income at all the honest answer is the ordinary tax itself (line 21 = line 1, so line 44 = line 46 = line 45), which is what sdtw-tax-unanswered-default-safe asserts at $0.
CONSUMER: exactly one, AND IT EXISTS — /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome in taxCalculations (SHIPPING, dictionary/ty2025/taxCalculations.xml), which takes this path on its gate-true arm. It must not acquire another: Form 1040 line 16 has a single home, and a duplicate global path for it is the defect that got the reference proposals refused. STILL NO Export element, and the reason has changed rather than expired. The old reason was "the consumer lands one commit later", which is spent; the standing reason is that the consumer now genuinely reads this fact, so the wiring obligation is discharged by real consumption rather than by a declared visibility marker. An Export added on top of that would assert a broader downstream surface than one consumer, and nothing needs it.
WORLD-1 SAFETY, AS THE COMMIT THAT WIRED IT LEFT THINGS. This fact used to move no return's tax because nothing read it; now the rebody does, and Form 1040 line 16 follows this worksheet whenever /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet is true. The gate-false population — the entire conformance corpus — keeps /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColA character for character, which is what made the switch an additions-only delta. On the gate-TRUE population the consequence to keep in view is that the $0 legs still carried by Schedule D line 19 are live under-statements of tax for any filer who has one, in the regular tax through this worksheet and in the AMT through form6251 Part III. SCHEDULE D LINE 18 IS NO LONGER AMONG THEM: the attestation pack fills every leg of its lines 1-4 subtotal. What line 18 can still get wrong runs the OTHER way — its line 5 is missing a SUBTRACTED Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 11 code D carryover, so that absence OVER-states line 18 and the 28% group.
COMPLETENESS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: Complete on 934 of the 938 resolved snapshots in the corpus, and the four it is absent from are EXACTLY the four /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColA is absent from (all four resolve /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColA Incomplete). Unconditional completeness is therefore NOT claimed: line 1 reads taxCalculations /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColA bare, exactly as /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine1ColA does, so a return that leaves /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColA Incomplete leaves this Incomplete too. That is the identical posture Form 1040 line 16 already has today, fact for fact, not a new hole.
CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST THE QDCGT ON THE WHOLE CORPUS, which is the strongest evidence this subtree has: when Schedule D lines 18 and 19 are both zero the SDTW degenerates to the QDCGT line for line (line 21 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine5ColA, 22 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine9ColA, 30 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine17ColA, 33 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine20ColA, 44 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine22ColA, 45 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine23ColA, 46 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine24ColA, and this fact = Round(/form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColA) — /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColA carries the same lesser-of UNROUNDED). All eight identities hold on 931 of 931 eligible snapshots against a separately authored shipping implementation. The three excluded snapshots are the divergence recorded in /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine7ColA's Description. The Form 2210 route gate excludes the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet; the Form 2555 parenthesis is not selected in this copy.

Fact.Name: Ordinary tax on Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 21 (worksheet line 44) — Schedule AI column (a)
Fact.Description:
The tax-rate-schedule tax on /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine21ColA, figured with the Tax Table / Tax Computation Worksheet exactly as Form 1040 line 16 is. This is Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 44.
THIS IS THE THIRD HARD-WIRED INSTANCE OF THE 2025 ORDINARY RATE SCHEDULE, and saying so plainly is part of this fact's contract rather than an apology for it. The other two are form2210 /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColA (over /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColA) and preferentialRateTax /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgOrdinaryTaxOnWorksheetOrdinaryIncomeColA (over the QDCGT's line-5 ordinary slice). The frozen engine has no function abstraction, so a single derivation cannot be parameterised by an arbitrary input amount and the bracket Switch has to be duplicated with its input swapped. GENERALISING THE RATE SCHEDULE INTO A REUSABLE HELPER IS A SEPARATE, LARGER REFACTOR AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT SMUGGLED INTO THIS UNIT: it would be an engine-shaped change touching every filing status of three shipping facts, and it belongs in its own unit with its own baseline diff.
ALL THREE SWITCHES MUST STAY IN SYNC, and this one is pinned to the first by an identity rather than by hand-copied numbers: whenever line 21 equals line 1 — which happens whenever no preferential dollar escapes the ordinary base — line 44 must equal line 46. sdtw-tax-boundary-line19-threshold-at-top is exactly that state at a nonzero amount (line 21 = line 1 = $197,300, line 44 = line 46 = $40,199), and sdtw-tax-unanswered-default-safe is the degenerate $0 form of it. The bracket boundaries and base-tax amounts here were COPIED mechanically from the QDCGT twin rather than retyped, so the three cannot differ by a typo.
ROUNDING: this fact applies its own Round, and that is the first of the two carve-outs the subtree's "one Round at line 47" rule names. A rate-schedule tax is a whole-dollar table lookup, so rounding it is part of computing it, not an early truncation of an intermediate. Line 46 inherits the identical carve-out from /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColA.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 19 threshold (top of the 24% ordinary bracket) — Schedule AI column (a)
Fact.Description:
The dollar amount named inside Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15: "$197,300 if single or married filing separately; $394,600 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse; or $197,300 if head of household."
THIS IS AN ORDINARY-RATE BOUNDARY, NOT A PREFERENTIAL ONE, which is the whole reason it is a new fact instead of a reuse. preferentialRateTax /qualDivCapGain0RateMax and /qualDivCapGain15RateMax come from Rev. Proc. 2024-40 section .03 (Maximum Capital Gains Rate); these two figures come from section .01 (Tax Rate Tables) and are EXACTLY the top of the 24% bracket in the 2025 rate schedule for every filing status — compare /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColA, whose single/MFS/HOH 24% case ends at $197,300 and whose MFJ/QSS 24% case ends at $394,600. Reusing a preferential-rate fact here would have been numerically wrong and conceptually worse.
THE IDENTITY IS DEFINITIONAL, NOT COINCIDENTAL, and it is worth stating because it explains what line 19 is doing. Unrecaptured section 1250 gain is taxed at the LESSER of 25% and the filer's ordinary rate, and 28%-rate gain at the lesser of 28% and the ordinary rate. Both caps can therefore only bite where the marginal ordinary rate first rises above them, and in a 10/12/22/24/32/35/37 schedule that point is the top of the 24% bracket. So the threshold moves with the ordinary bracket, and must: it is the same figure, not a parallel one. The param annotations below deliberately name the EXISTING bracket-top ledger rows rather than minting new ids, so the two can never drift apart.
MFS TAKES THE SINGLE/HOH AMOUNT HERE, unlike the 15%-rate maximum (where MFS is $300,000, half of MFJ). That asymmetry is the source's own — it prints $197,300 for single, MFS and head of household alike — and it matches the ordinary rate schedule, where MFS shares the single 24% bracket top.

STRUCTURAL TWIN of both of those (the engine has no taxOnAmount(x) primitive, so the midpoint Switch is duplicated with its input swapped); all three MUST stay in sync.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 47 — tax on all taxable income — Schedule AI column (b)
Fact.Description:
THE SCHEDULE D TAX WORKSHEET'S FINAL TAX, and the root of the /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine1ColB through /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine46ColB subtree above. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Tax on all taxable income (including capital gains and qualified dividends). Enter the smaller of line 45 or line 46. Also, include this amount on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 16. (If you are filing Form 2555, don't enter this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16. Instead, enter it on line 4 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040.)" This fact IS line 47; there is no separate /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine4ColB7, exactly as /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColB is both the QDCGT's last line and its output.
THE SINGLE ROUND OF THE WHOLE WORKSHEET SITS HERE, matching /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColB's sibling treatment: the per-line children stay unrounded so the 15%, 20%, 25% and 28% multiplications (lines 31, 34, 40 and 43) do not each accumulate a rounding error before line 45 sums them. TWO EXCEPTIONS, stated so the claim is not read as absolute — lines 44 and 46 are rate-schedule taxes and each arrives already rounded from the fact that computes it (/form2210ScheduleAiSdtwOrdinaryTaxOnLine21ColB and form2210 /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColB). Rounding a whole-dollar table lookup is part of computing it, not an early truncation of an intermediate.
THAT PRE-ROUNDING IS NOT COSMETIC, and the tests say so: on sdtw-tax-boundary-line19-threshold-one-dollar-over, line 45 is $40,199.25 and line 46 is $40,199, so the lesser-of picks line 46 — the extra dollar's 25% tax loses to a line 46 that was rounded down from $40,199.32. A reviewer changing where the Round sits will break that case, which is the point of it.
THE FORM 2555 CARVE-OUT, BOTH HALVES, AND BOTH ARE NOW IMPLEMENTED — BY A SECOND WORKSHEET, NOT BY THIS ONE. Line 47's own text redirects the RESULT away from Form 1040 line 16 for a Form 2555 filer, and worksheet line 1 (:1084-1086) redirects the INPUT the same way ("if you are filing Form 2555 ... enter instead the amount from line 3 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet"); the same footnote hangs off lines 6, 9 and 11 (:1173-1174). The footnote does not ask this worksheet to change — it asks for a SECOND run, "in its entirety and with the following additional modifications" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37), whose modifications are "to be made only for purposes of filling out the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet above". That second run is /feiScheduleDTaxWorksheetTax and the /feiSdtw* lineage below, and its root is taken by preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4 on the arm that fires on /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet. THIS fact is the first run and keeps its unsubstituted input and its Form 1040 line 16 destination, which is right for every filer who is not completing that worksheet — and for the filer who is, taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome pre-empts the arm that reads this fact, so it never figures line 16 for them.
COMPUTED ON EVERY RETURN, DELIBERATELY. /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet is NOT a term of this fact: it decides WHICH worksheet figures Form 1040 line 16, and that decision belongs to the consumer. Gating this fact on it would make the SDTW resolve to a fictitious $0 on every QDCGT return, which is worse than an honest "what the SDTW would produce". On a return with no preferential income at all the honest answer is the ordinary tax itself (line 21 = line 1, so line 44 = line 46 = line 45), which is what sdtw-tax-unanswered-default-safe asserts at $0.
CONSUMER: exactly one, AND IT EXISTS — /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome in taxCalculations (SHIPPING, dictionary/ty2025/taxCalculations.xml), which takes this path on its gate-true arm. It must not acquire another: Form 1040 line 16 has a single home, and a duplicate global path for it is the defect that got the reference proposals refused. STILL NO Export element, and the reason has changed rather than expired. The old reason was "the consumer lands one commit later", which is spent; the standing reason is that the consumer now genuinely reads this fact, so the wiring obligation is discharged by real consumption rather than by a declared visibility marker. An Export added on top of that would assert a broader downstream surface than one consumer, and nothing needs it.
WORLD-1 SAFETY, AS THE COMMIT THAT WIRED IT LEFT THINGS. This fact used to move no return's tax because nothing read it; now the rebody does, and Form 1040 line 16 follows this worksheet whenever /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet is true. The gate-false population — the entire conformance corpus — keeps /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColB character for character, which is what made the switch an additions-only delta. On the gate-TRUE population the consequence to keep in view is that the $0 legs still carried by Schedule D line 19 are live under-statements of tax for any filer who has one, in the regular tax through this worksheet and in the AMT through form6251 Part III. SCHEDULE D LINE 18 IS NO LONGER AMONG THEM: the attestation pack fills every leg of its lines 1-4 subtotal. What line 18 can still get wrong runs the OTHER way — its line 5 is missing a SUBTRACTED Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 11 code D carryover, so that absence OVER-states line 18 and the 28% group.
COMPLETENESS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: Complete on 934 of the 938 resolved snapshots in the corpus, and the four it is absent from are EXACTLY the four /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColB is absent from (all four resolve /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColB Incomplete). Unconditional completeness is therefore NOT claimed: line 1 reads taxCalculations /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColB bare, exactly as /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine1ColB does, so a return that leaves /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColB Incomplete leaves this Incomplete too. That is the identical posture Form 1040 line 16 already has today, fact for fact, not a new hole.
CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST THE QDCGT ON THE WHOLE CORPUS, which is the strongest evidence this subtree has: when Schedule D lines 18 and 19 are both zero the SDTW degenerates to the QDCGT line for line (line 21 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine5ColB, 22 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine9ColB, 30 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine17ColB, 33 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine20ColB, 44 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine22ColB, 45 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine23ColB, 46 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine24ColB, and this fact = Round(/form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColB) — /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColB carries the same lesser-of UNROUNDED). All eight identities hold on 931 of 931 eligible snapshots against a separately authored shipping implementation. The three excluded snapshots are the divergence recorded in /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine7ColB's Description. The Form 2210 route gate excludes the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet; the Form 2555 parenthesis is not selected in this copy.

Fact.Name: Ordinary tax on Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 21 (worksheet line 44) — Schedule AI column (b)
Fact.Description:
The tax-rate-schedule tax on /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine21ColB, figured with the Tax Table / Tax Computation Worksheet exactly as Form 1040 line 16 is. This is Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 44.
THIS IS THE THIRD HARD-WIRED INSTANCE OF THE 2025 ORDINARY RATE SCHEDULE, and saying so plainly is part of this fact's contract rather than an apology for it. The other two are form2210 /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColB (over /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColB) and preferentialRateTax /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgOrdinaryTaxOnWorksheetOrdinaryIncomeColB (over the QDCGT's line-5 ordinary slice). The frozen engine has no function abstraction, so a single derivation cannot be parameterised by an arbitrary input amount and the bracket Switch has to be duplicated with its input swapped. GENERALISING THE RATE SCHEDULE INTO A REUSABLE HELPER IS A SEPARATE, LARGER REFACTOR AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT SMUGGLED INTO THIS UNIT: it would be an engine-shaped change touching every filing status of three shipping facts, and it belongs in its own unit with its own baseline diff.
ALL THREE SWITCHES MUST STAY IN SYNC, and this one is pinned to the first by an identity rather than by hand-copied numbers: whenever line 21 equals line 1 — which happens whenever no preferential dollar escapes the ordinary base — line 44 must equal line 46. sdtw-tax-boundary-line19-threshold-at-top is exactly that state at a nonzero amount (line 21 = line 1 = $197,300, line 44 = line 46 = $40,199), and sdtw-tax-unanswered-default-safe is the degenerate $0 form of it. The bracket boundaries and base-tax amounts here were COPIED mechanically from the QDCGT twin rather than retyped, so the three cannot differ by a typo.
ROUNDING: this fact applies its own Round, and that is the first of the two carve-outs the subtree's "one Round at line 47" rule names. A rate-schedule tax is a whole-dollar table lookup, so rounding it is part of computing it, not an early truncation of an intermediate. Line 46 inherits the identical carve-out from /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColB.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 19 threshold (top of the 24% ordinary bracket) — Schedule AI column (b)
Fact.Description:
The dollar amount named inside Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15: "$197,300 if single or married filing separately; $394,600 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse; or $197,300 if head of household."
THIS IS AN ORDINARY-RATE BOUNDARY, NOT A PREFERENTIAL ONE, which is the whole reason it is a new fact instead of a reuse. preferentialRateTax /qualDivCapGain0RateMax and /qualDivCapGain15RateMax come from Rev. Proc. 2024-40 section .03 (Maximum Capital Gains Rate); these two figures come from section .01 (Tax Rate Tables) and are EXACTLY the top of the 24% bracket in the 2025 rate schedule for every filing status — compare /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColB, whose single/MFS/HOH 24% case ends at $197,300 and whose MFJ/QSS 24% case ends at $394,600. Reusing a preferential-rate fact here would have been numerically wrong and conceptually worse.
THE IDENTITY IS DEFINITIONAL, NOT COINCIDENTAL, and it is worth stating because it explains what line 19 is doing. Unrecaptured section 1250 gain is taxed at the LESSER of 25% and the filer's ordinary rate, and 28%-rate gain at the lesser of 28% and the ordinary rate. Both caps can therefore only bite where the marginal ordinary rate first rises above them, and in a 10/12/22/24/32/35/37 schedule that point is the top of the 24% bracket. So the threshold moves with the ordinary bracket, and must: it is the same figure, not a parallel one. The param annotations below deliberately name the EXISTING bracket-top ledger rows rather than minting new ids, so the two can never drift apart.
MFS TAKES THE SINGLE/HOH AMOUNT HERE, unlike the 15%-rate maximum (where MFS is $300,000, half of MFJ). That asymmetry is the source's own — it prints $197,300 for single, MFS and head of household alike — and it matches the ordinary rate schedule, where MFS shares the single 24% bracket top.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 47 — tax on all taxable income — Schedule AI column (c)
Fact.Description:
THE SCHEDULE D TAX WORKSHEET'S FINAL TAX, and the root of the /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine1ColC through /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine46ColC subtree above. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Tax on all taxable income (including capital gains and qualified dividends). Enter the smaller of line 45 or line 46. Also, include this amount on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 16. (If you are filing Form 2555, don't enter this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16. Instead, enter it on line 4 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040.)" This fact IS line 47; there is no separate /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine4ColC7, exactly as /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColC is both the QDCGT's last line and its output.
THE SINGLE ROUND OF THE WHOLE WORKSHEET SITS HERE, matching /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColC's sibling treatment: the per-line children stay unrounded so the 15%, 20%, 25% and 28% multiplications (lines 31, 34, 40 and 43) do not each accumulate a rounding error before line 45 sums them. TWO EXCEPTIONS, stated so the claim is not read as absolute — lines 44 and 46 are rate-schedule taxes and each arrives already rounded from the fact that computes it (/form2210ScheduleAiSdtwOrdinaryTaxOnLine21ColC and form2210 /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColC). Rounding a whole-dollar table lookup is part of computing it, not an early truncation of an intermediate.
THAT PRE-ROUNDING IS NOT COSMETIC, and the tests say so: on sdtw-tax-boundary-line19-threshold-one-dollar-over, line 45 is $40,199.25 and line 46 is $40,199, so the lesser-of picks line 46 — the extra dollar's 25% tax loses to a line 46 that was rounded down from $40,199.32. A reviewer changing where the Round sits will break that case, which is the point of it.
THE FORM 2555 CARVE-OUT, BOTH HALVES, AND BOTH ARE NOW IMPLEMENTED — BY A SECOND WORKSHEET, NOT BY THIS ONE. Line 47's own text redirects the RESULT away from Form 1040 line 16 for a Form 2555 filer, and worksheet line 1 (:1084-1086) redirects the INPUT the same way ("if you are filing Form 2555 ... enter instead the amount from line 3 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet"); the same footnote hangs off lines 6, 9 and 11 (:1173-1174). The footnote does not ask this worksheet to change — it asks for a SECOND run, "in its entirety and with the following additional modifications" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37), whose modifications are "to be made only for purposes of filling out the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet above". That second run is /feiScheduleDTaxWorksheetTax and the /feiSdtw* lineage below, and its root is taken by preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4 on the arm that fires on /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet. THIS fact is the first run and keeps its unsubstituted input and its Form 1040 line 16 destination, which is right for every filer who is not completing that worksheet — and for the filer who is, taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome pre-empts the arm that reads this fact, so it never figures line 16 for them.
COMPUTED ON EVERY RETURN, DELIBERATELY. /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet is NOT a term of this fact: it decides WHICH worksheet figures Form 1040 line 16, and that decision belongs to the consumer. Gating this fact on it would make the SDTW resolve to a fictitious $0 on every QDCGT return, which is worse than an honest "what the SDTW would produce". On a return with no preferential income at all the honest answer is the ordinary tax itself (line 21 = line 1, so line 44 = line 46 = line 45), which is what sdtw-tax-unanswered-default-safe asserts at $0.
CONSUMER: exactly one, AND IT EXISTS — /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome in taxCalculations (SHIPPING, dictionary/ty2025/taxCalculations.xml), which takes this path on its gate-true arm. It must not acquire another: Form 1040 line 16 has a single home, and a duplicate global path for it is the defect that got the reference proposals refused. STILL NO Export element, and the reason has changed rather than expired. The old reason was "the consumer lands one commit later", which is spent; the standing reason is that the consumer now genuinely reads this fact, so the wiring obligation is discharged by real consumption rather than by a declared visibility marker. An Export added on top of that would assert a broader downstream surface than one consumer, and nothing needs it.
WORLD-1 SAFETY, AS THE COMMIT THAT WIRED IT LEFT THINGS. This fact used to move no return's tax because nothing read it; now the rebody does, and Form 1040 line 16 follows this worksheet whenever /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet is true. The gate-false population — the entire conformance corpus — keeps /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColC character for character, which is what made the switch an additions-only delta. On the gate-TRUE population the consequence to keep in view is that the $0 legs still carried by Schedule D line 19 are live under-statements of tax for any filer who has one, in the regular tax through this worksheet and in the AMT through form6251 Part III. SCHEDULE D LINE 18 IS NO LONGER AMONG THEM: the attestation pack fills every leg of its lines 1-4 subtotal. What line 18 can still get wrong runs the OTHER way — its line 5 is missing a SUBTRACTED Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 11 code D carryover, so that absence OVER-states line 18 and the 28% group.
COMPLETENESS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: Complete on 934 of the 938 resolved snapshots in the corpus, and the four it is absent from are EXACTLY the four /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColC is absent from (all four resolve /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColC Incomplete). Unconditional completeness is therefore NOT claimed: line 1 reads taxCalculations /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColC bare, exactly as /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine1ColC does, so a return that leaves /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColC Incomplete leaves this Incomplete too. That is the identical posture Form 1040 line 16 already has today, fact for fact, not a new hole.
CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST THE QDCGT ON THE WHOLE CORPUS, which is the strongest evidence this subtree has: when Schedule D lines 18 and 19 are both zero the SDTW degenerates to the QDCGT line for line (line 21 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine5ColC, 22 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine9ColC, 30 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine17ColC, 33 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine20ColC, 44 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine22ColC, 45 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine23ColC, 46 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine24ColC, and this fact = Round(/form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColC) — /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColC carries the same lesser-of UNROUNDED). All eight identities hold on 931 of 931 eligible snapshots against a separately authored shipping implementation. The three excluded snapshots are the divergence recorded in /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine7ColC's Description. The Form 2210 route gate excludes the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet; the Form 2555 parenthesis is not selected in this copy.

Fact.Name: Ordinary tax on Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 21 (worksheet line 44) — Schedule AI column (c)
Fact.Description:
The tax-rate-schedule tax on /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine21ColC, figured with the Tax Table / Tax Computation Worksheet exactly as Form 1040 line 16 is. This is Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 44.
THIS IS THE THIRD HARD-WIRED INSTANCE OF THE 2025 ORDINARY RATE SCHEDULE, and saying so plainly is part of this fact's contract rather than an apology for it. The other two are form2210 /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColC (over /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColC) and preferentialRateTax /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgOrdinaryTaxOnWorksheetOrdinaryIncomeColC (over the QDCGT's line-5 ordinary slice). The frozen engine has no function abstraction, so a single derivation cannot be parameterised by an arbitrary input amount and the bracket Switch has to be duplicated with its input swapped. GENERALISING THE RATE SCHEDULE INTO A REUSABLE HELPER IS A SEPARATE, LARGER REFACTOR AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT SMUGGLED INTO THIS UNIT: it would be an engine-shaped change touching every filing status of three shipping facts, and it belongs in its own unit with its own baseline diff.
ALL THREE SWITCHES MUST STAY IN SYNC, and this one is pinned to the first by an identity rather than by hand-copied numbers: whenever line 21 equals line 1 — which happens whenever no preferential dollar escapes the ordinary base — line 44 must equal line 46. sdtw-tax-boundary-line19-threshold-at-top is exactly that state at a nonzero amount (line 21 = line 1 = $197,300, line 44 = line 46 = $40,199), and sdtw-tax-unanswered-default-safe is the degenerate $0 form of it. The bracket boundaries and base-tax amounts here were COPIED mechanically from the QDCGT twin rather than retyped, so the three cannot differ by a typo.
ROUNDING: this fact applies its own Round, and that is the first of the two carve-outs the subtree's "one Round at line 47" rule names. A rate-schedule tax is a whole-dollar table lookup, so rounding it is part of computing it, not an early truncation of an intermediate. Line 46 inherits the identical carve-out from /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColC.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 19 threshold (top of the 24% ordinary bracket) — Schedule AI column (c)
Fact.Description:
The dollar amount named inside Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15: "$197,300 if single or married filing separately; $394,600 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse; or $197,300 if head of household."
THIS IS AN ORDINARY-RATE BOUNDARY, NOT A PREFERENTIAL ONE, which is the whole reason it is a new fact instead of a reuse. preferentialRateTax /qualDivCapGain0RateMax and /qualDivCapGain15RateMax come from Rev. Proc. 2024-40 section .03 (Maximum Capital Gains Rate); these two figures come from section .01 (Tax Rate Tables) and are EXACTLY the top of the 24% bracket in the 2025 rate schedule for every filing status — compare /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColC, whose single/MFS/HOH 24% case ends at $197,300 and whose MFJ/QSS 24% case ends at $394,600. Reusing a preferential-rate fact here would have been numerically wrong and conceptually worse.
THE IDENTITY IS DEFINITIONAL, NOT COINCIDENTAL, and it is worth stating because it explains what line 19 is doing. Unrecaptured section 1250 gain is taxed at the LESSER of 25% and the filer's ordinary rate, and 28%-rate gain at the lesser of 28% and the ordinary rate. Both caps can therefore only bite where the marginal ordinary rate first rises above them, and in a 10/12/22/24/32/35/37 schedule that point is the top of the 24% bracket. So the threshold moves with the ordinary bracket, and must: it is the same figure, not a parallel one. The param annotations below deliberately name the EXISTING bracket-top ledger rows rather than minting new ids, so the two can never drift apart.
MFS TAKES THE SINGLE/HOH AMOUNT HERE, unlike the 15%-rate maximum (where MFS is $300,000, half of MFJ). That asymmetry is the source's own — it prints $197,300 for single, MFS and head of household alike — and it matches the ordinary rate schedule, where MFS shares the single 24% bracket top.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 47 — tax on all taxable income — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description:
THE SCHEDULE D TAX WORKSHEET'S FINAL TAX, and the root of the /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine1ColD through /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine46ColD subtree above. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Tax on all taxable income (including capital gains and qualified dividends). Enter the smaller of line 45 or line 46. Also, include this amount on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 16. (If you are filing Form 2555, don't enter this amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16. Instead, enter it on line 4 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040.)" This fact IS line 47; there is no separate /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine4ColD7, exactly as /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColD is both the QDCGT's last line and its output.
THE SINGLE ROUND OF THE WHOLE WORKSHEET SITS HERE, matching /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColD's sibling treatment: the per-line children stay unrounded so the 15%, 20%, 25% and 28% multiplications (lines 31, 34, 40 and 43) do not each accumulate a rounding error before line 45 sums them. TWO EXCEPTIONS, stated so the claim is not read as absolute — lines 44 and 46 are rate-schedule taxes and each arrives already rounded from the fact that computes it (/form2210ScheduleAiSdtwOrdinaryTaxOnLine21ColD and form2210 /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColD). Rounding a whole-dollar table lookup is part of computing it, not an early truncation of an intermediate.
THAT PRE-ROUNDING IS NOT COSMETIC, and the tests say so: on sdtw-tax-boundary-line19-threshold-one-dollar-over, line 45 is $40,199.25 and line 46 is $40,199, so the lesser-of picks line 46 — the extra dollar's 25% tax loses to a line 46 that was rounded down from $40,199.32. A reviewer changing where the Round sits will break that case, which is the point of it.
THE FORM 2555 CARVE-OUT, BOTH HALVES, AND BOTH ARE NOW IMPLEMENTED — BY A SECOND WORKSHEET, NOT BY THIS ONE. Line 47's own text redirects the RESULT away from Form 1040 line 16 for a Form 2555 filer, and worksheet line 1 (:1084-1086) redirects the INPUT the same way ("if you are filing Form 2555 ... enter instead the amount from line 3 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet"); the same footnote hangs off lines 6, 9 and 11 (:1173-1174). The footnote does not ask this worksheet to change — it asks for a SECOND run, "in its entirety and with the following additional modifications" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 37), whose modifications are "to be made only for purposes of filling out the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet above". That second run is /feiScheduleDTaxWorksheetTax and the /feiSdtw* lineage below, and its root is taken by preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine4 on the arm that fires on /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet. THIS fact is the first run and keeps its unsubstituted input and its Form 1040 line 16 destination, which is right for every filer who is not completing that worksheet — and for the filer who is, taxCalculations /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome pre-empts the arm that reads this fact, so it never figures line 16 for them.
COMPUTED ON EVERY RETURN, DELIBERATELY. /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet is NOT a term of this fact: it decides WHICH worksheet figures Form 1040 line 16, and that decision belongs to the consumer. Gating this fact on it would make the SDTW resolve to a fictitious $0 on every QDCGT return, which is worse than an honest "what the SDTW would produce". On a return with no preferential income at all the honest answer is the ordinary tax itself (line 21 = line 1, so line 44 = line 46 = line 45), which is what sdtw-tax-unanswered-default-safe asserts at $0.
CONSUMER: exactly one, AND IT EXISTS — /tentativeTaxFromTaxableIncome in taxCalculations (SHIPPING, dictionary/ty2025/taxCalculations.xml), which takes this path on its gate-true arm. It must not acquire another: Form 1040 line 16 has a single home, and a duplicate global path for it is the defect that got the reference proposals refused. STILL NO Export element, and the reason has changed rather than expired. The old reason was "the consumer lands one commit later", which is spent; the standing reason is that the consumer now genuinely reads this fact, so the wiring obligation is discharged by real consumption rather than by a declared visibility marker. An Export added on top of that would assert a broader downstream surface than one consumer, and nothing needs it.
WORLD-1 SAFETY, AS THE COMMIT THAT WIRED IT LEFT THINGS. This fact used to move no return's tax because nothing read it; now the rebody does, and Form 1040 line 16 follows this worksheet whenever /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet is true. The gate-false population — the entire conformance corpus — keeps /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColD character for character, which is what made the switch an additions-only delta. On the gate-TRUE population the consequence to keep in view is that the $0 legs still carried by Schedule D line 19 are live under-statements of tax for any filer who has one, in the regular tax through this worksheet and in the AMT through form6251 Part III. SCHEDULE D LINE 18 IS NO LONGER AMONG THEM: the attestation pack fills every leg of its lines 1-4 subtotal. What line 18 can still get wrong runs the OTHER way — its line 5 is missing a SUBTRACTED Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 11 code D carryover, so that absence OVER-states line 18 and the 28% group.
COMPLETENESS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: Complete on 934 of the 938 resolved snapshots in the corpus, and the four it is absent from are EXACTLY the four /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColD is absent from (all four resolve /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColD Incomplete). Unconditional completeness is therefore NOT claimed: line 1 reads taxCalculations /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColD bare, exactly as /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine1ColD does, so a return that leaves /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColD Incomplete leaves this Incomplete too. That is the identical posture Form 1040 line 16 already has today, fact for fact, not a new hole.
CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST THE QDCGT ON THE WHOLE CORPUS, which is the strongest evidence this subtree has: when Schedule D lines 18 and 19 are both zero the SDTW degenerates to the QDCGT line for line (line 21 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine5ColD, 22 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine9ColD, 30 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine17ColD, 33 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine20ColD, 44 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine22ColD, 45 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine23ColD, 46 = /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine24ColD, and this fact = Round(/form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColD) — /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine25ColD carries the same lesser-of UNROUNDED). All eight identities hold on 931 of 931 eligible snapshots against a separately authored shipping implementation. The three excluded snapshots are the divergence recorded in /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine7ColD's Description. The Form 2210 route gate excludes the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet; the Form 2555 parenthesis is not selected in this copy.

Fact.Name: Ordinary tax on Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 21 (worksheet line 44) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description:
The tax-rate-schedule tax on /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine21ColD, figured with the Tax Table / Tax Computation Worksheet exactly as Form 1040 line 16 is. This is Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 44.
THIS IS THE THIRD HARD-WIRED INSTANCE OF THE 2025 ORDINARY RATE SCHEDULE, and saying so plainly is part of this fact's contract rather than an apology for it. The other two are form2210 /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColD (over /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColD) and preferentialRateTax /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgOrdinaryTaxOnWorksheetOrdinaryIncomeColD (over the QDCGT's line-5 ordinary slice). The frozen engine has no function abstraction, so a single derivation cannot be parameterised by an arbitrary input amount and the bracket Switch has to be duplicated with its input swapped. GENERALISING THE RATE SCHEDULE INTO A REUSABLE HELPER IS A SEPARATE, LARGER REFACTOR AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT SMUGGLED INTO THIS UNIT: it would be an engine-shaped change touching every filing status of three shipping facts, and it belongs in its own unit with its own baseline diff.
ALL THREE SWITCHES MUST STAY IN SYNC, and this one is pinned to the first by an identity rather than by hand-copied numbers: whenever line 21 equals line 1 — which happens whenever no preferential dollar escapes the ordinary base — line 44 must equal line 46. sdtw-tax-boundary-line19-threshold-at-top is exactly that state at a nonzero amount (line 21 = line 1 = $197,300, line 44 = line 46 = $40,199), and sdtw-tax-unanswered-default-safe is the degenerate $0 form of it. The bracket boundaries and base-tax amounts here were COPIED mechanically from the QDCGT twin rather than retyped, so the three cannot differ by a typo.
ROUNDING: this fact applies its own Round, and that is the first of the two carve-outs the subtree's "one Round at line 47" rule names. A rate-schedule tax is a whole-dollar table lookup, so rounding it is part of computing it, not an early truncation of an intermediate. Line 46 inherits the identical carve-out from /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColD.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 19 threshold (top of the 24% ordinary bracket) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description:
The dollar amount named inside Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 19, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15: "$197,300 if single or married filing separately; $394,600 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse; or $197,300 if head of household."
THIS IS AN ORDINARY-RATE BOUNDARY, NOT A PREFERENTIAL ONE, which is the whole reason it is a new fact instead of a reuse. preferentialRateTax /qualDivCapGain0RateMax and /qualDivCapGain15RateMax come from Rev. Proc. 2024-40 section .03 (Maximum Capital Gains Rate); these two figures come from section .01 (Tax Rate Tables) and are EXACTLY the top of the 24% bracket in the 2025 rate schedule for every filing status — compare /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColD, whose single/MFS/HOH 24% case ends at $197,300 and whose MFJ/QSS 24% case ends at $394,600. Reusing a preferential-rate fact here would have been numerically wrong and conceptually worse.
THE IDENTITY IS DEFINITIONAL, NOT COINCIDENTAL, and it is worth stating because it explains what line 19 is doing. Unrecaptured section 1250 gain is taxed at the LESSER of 25% and the filer's ordinary rate, and 28%-rate gain at the lesser of 28% and the ordinary rate. Both caps can therefore only bite where the marginal ordinary rate first rises above them, and in a 10/12/22/24/32/35/37 schedule that point is the top of the 24% bracket. So the threshold moves with the ordinary bracket, and must: it is the same figure, not a parallel one. The param annotations below deliberately name the EXISTING bracket-top ledger rows rather than minting new ids, so the two can never drift apart.
MFS TAKES THE SINGLE/HOH AMOUNT HERE, unlike the 15%-rate maximum (where MFS is $300,000, half of MFJ). That asymmetry is the source's own — it prints $197,300 for single, MFS and head of household alike — and it matches the ordinary rate schedule, where MFS shares the single 24% bracket top.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 21 at its Tax Table row midpoint — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: The Tax Table row midpoint of /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwLine21ColD, exactly as taxCalculations /form2210ScheduleAiLine13RoundedColD does for /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColD and preferentialRateTax /worksheetOrdinaryIncomeRounded does for the QDCGT's ordinary slice. Drives line 44 (the tax on line 21). STRUCTURAL TWIN of both of those (the engine has no taxOnAmount(x) primitive, so the midpoint Switch is duplicated with its input swapped); all three MUST stay in sync.
