Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the larger of line 18 or line 20". This is the amount line 44 taxes at ordinary rates — the taxable income that is either genuinely ordinary (line 18) or preferential income sitting below the point where the 25%/28% caps beat the ordinary rate (line 20).

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 22 (amount taxed at 0%) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 17 from line 16. This amount is taxed at 0%". Never negative: line 17 is a LesserOf with line 16 as an operand.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 23 — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 1 or line 13". The instruction immediately above it (:1126) reads "If lines 1 and 16 are the same, skip lines 23 through 43 and go to line 44"; that skip is not encoded, because the arithmetic already zeroes lines 31, 34, 40 and 43 in that case (the block header above carries the proof).

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 24 — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the amount from line 22. (If line 22 is blank, enter -0-.)" Line 22 is a computed fact here and is never blank, so the parenthesis is satisfied structurally.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 25 — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 24 from line 23. If zero or less, enter -0-". The floor never actually bites: line 23 is always at least line 24 (the block header proves L23 >= L22 = L24), which is what keeps line 33 non-negative downstream.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 26 (15%-rate bracket top) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter: $533,400 if single; $300,000 if married filing separately; $600,050 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse; or $566,700 if head of household." Those are EXACTLY the figures preferentialRateTax /qualDivCapGain15RateMax already carries for QDCGT line 13, so this line REUSES that fact. Note that MFS is $300,000 here — half the MFJ amount — which is why this line and line 19 cannot share a threshold fact.

Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 1 or line 26".

Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Multiply line 30 by 15% (0.15)". UNROUNDED, deliberately: rounding here instead of at line 47 would let each of the four rate multiplications accumulate its own error.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 32 — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Add lines 24 and 30". The instruction below it (:1144) reads "If lines 1 and 32 are the same, skip lines 33 through 43 and go to line 44"; not encoded, because line 1 equal to line 32 forces line 33 to zero and the 25%/28% groups with it (proof in the block header).

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 33 (amount taxed at 20%) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Subtract line 32 from line 23". THE SOURCE GIVES THIS LINE NO FLOOR and it does not need one: line 33 equals line 25 less line 30, line 30 is a LesserOf with line 25 as an operand, so line 33 is max(line 25 - line 29, 0) and is never negative. The block header carries the L23 >= L22 step that argument rests on.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 34 (tax at 20%) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Multiply line 33 by 20% (0.20)". Unrounded, as line 31.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 35 (the 25% group begins) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 9 above or Schedule D, line 19". SCHEDULE D line 19 is /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwUnrecapturedSection1250GainColD — the shipping worksheet, not this worksheet's own line 19.
THE GATE ABOVE THIS LINE (:1147), "If Schedule D, line 19, is zero or blank, skip lines 35 through 40 and go to line 41", IS NOT ENCODED and does not need to be: a zero Schedule D line 19 makes this line the smaller of line 9 and $0, hence $0, and line 39 then floors to $0 because line 38 is never negative. The sdtw-tax-28-percent-group-derived-example case is exactly that state (Schedule D line 19 = $0) and asserts lines 35 through 40 at zero.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 36 — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Add lines 10 and 21".

Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Enter the amount from line 1 above". A restatement of line 1 so line 38 can subtract it; kept as its own fact because the worksheet numbers it.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 38 — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Subtract line 37 from line 36. If zero or less, enter -0-". How much of the unrecaptured section 1250 gain sits BELOW the point where the 25% cap beats the ordinary rate, and is therefore taxed inside line 21 instead.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 39 (amount taxed at 25%) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Subtract line 38 from line 35. If zero or less, enter -0-". The unrecaptured section 1250 gain that actually reaches the 25% rate — which is only the part above the line-19 threshold, because below it line 38 grows to swallow line 35 exactly. The sdtw-tax-boundary-line19-threshold-* pair pins that activation point: $0 at the threshold, $1 one dollar over.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 40 (tax at 25%) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Multiply line 39 by 25% (0.25)". Unrounded, as lines 31 and 34.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 41 (the 28% group begins) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description:
https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Add lines 21, 22, 30, 33, and 39". Every dollar of taxable income already assigned to a rate: the ordinary base, the 0% slice, the 15% slice, the 20% slice and the 25% slice.
THE GATE ABOVE THIS LINE (:1154), "If Schedule D, line 18, is zero or blank, skip lines 41 through 43 and go to line 44", IS NOT ENCODED. A zero SCHEDULE D line 18 makes line 42 identically zero — that is the least obvious of the four skip proofs and the block header carries it in full. The sdtw-tax-25-percent-group-derived-example case is exactly that state (Schedule D line 18 = $0) and asserts lines 41 through 43 accordingly.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 42 (amount taxed at 28%) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Subtract line 41 from line 1". THE SOURCE GIVES THIS LINE NO FLOOR EITHER, and again it does not need one: substituting line 41's collapse (line 21 + line 23 + line 39) shows line 42 is never negative, and is identically zero whenever Schedule D line 18 is zero. Both steps are in the block header.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 43 (tax at 28%) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Multiply line 42 by 28% (0.28)". Unrounded, as lines 31, 34 and 40 — the last of the four multiplications the single Round at line 47 exists to protect.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 44 (tax on line 21) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Figure the tax on the amount on line 21. If the amount on line 21 is less than $100,000, use the Tax Table to figure the tax. If the amount on line 21 is $100,000 or more, use the Tax Computation Worksheet." That is /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwOrdinaryTaxOnLine21ColD above — the third hard-wired instance of the 2025 ordinary rate schedule, which that fact's Description explains and justifies. Arrives ALREADY ROUNDED; see the rounding carve-out there.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 45 (the worksheet tax) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Add lines 31, 34, 40, 43, and 44". The four rate multiplications still carry their cents at this point; only line 44 is pre-rounded. THIS is the sum the subtree's single Round exists to protect.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 46 (tax on line 1) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 16, verbatim: "Figure the tax on the amount on line 1. If the amount on line 1 is less than $100,000, use the Tax Table to figure the tax. If the amount on line 1 is $100,000 or more, use the Tax Computation Worksheet." Line 1 is taxable income, so this is EXACTLY taxCalculations /form2210ScheduleAiOrdinaryTaxOnLine13ColD, REUSED — the same fact /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine24ColD reads for the QDCGT's identical line. THE SECOND ROUNDING CARVE-OUT: that fact applies its own Round internally (dictionary/ty2025/taxCalculations.xml, Derived/Round/Switch), so line 46 arrives already rounded and this subtree inherits it. Consistent, not a conflict, for the same reason as line 44.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 1 (taxable income) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter your taxable income from Schedule AI line 13. (However, if you are filing Form 2555 (relating to foreign earned income), enter instead the amount from line 3 of the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the instructions for Form 1040, line 16.)" form2210 /form2210ScheduleAiLine13ColD, read bare exactly as /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine1ColD reads it. THE FORM 2555 REDIRECT IS IMPLEMENTED, AND NOT HERE: this fact is the FIRST run's line 1, the unsubstituted taxable income that figures Form 1040 line 16 for every filer who is not completing the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet. The substitution lives on /feiSdtwLine1, the second run's line 1, which takes preferentialRateTax /foreignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine3. THIS fact is also what the capital gain excess is measured against, because the footnote's subtrahend is Schedule AI line 13 itself — see /feiSdtwCapitalGainExcess. The root fact /form2210ScheduleAiSdtwTaxColD states the routing of both halves.

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 2 (qualified dividends) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter your qualified dividends from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 3a". income /form2210ScheduleAiQualifiedDividendsColD, the same fact /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine2ColD reads — and read DIRECTLY, not through /form2210ScheduleAiQdcgLine2ColD itself. Aliasing the QDCGT's line 2 would couple this worksheet to the other worksheet's internal line numbering for no gain; the two worksheets share an INPUT, not a line.

Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 4 from line 3. If zero or less, enter -0-".

Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 5 from line 2. If zero or less, enter -0-**". The double asterisk is the Form 2555 footnote (:1173-1174), and it IS implemented — on the SECOND run, as /feiSdtwLine6, where modification (2) reduces this amount by the unused capital gain excess. Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Enter the smaller of line 3 or line 4".

Fact.Name: Schedule D Tax Worksheet line 9 (net capital gain slice) — Schedule AI column (d)
Fact.Description: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 15, verbatim: "Subtract line 8 from line 7. If zero or less, enter -0-**". The floor is what makes a Schedule D LOSS on line 7 harmless here. The double asterisk is the Form 2555 footnote (:1173-1174), implemented on the SECOND run as /feiSdtwLine9 (modification (1)); this fact is the first run's line 9, and it is also both the "amount you would otherwise enter" that modification reduces and the amount /feiSdtwCapitalGainExcessNotUsedAgainstLine9 measures the leftover against.
